title: パターン別徹底ドリル N1

items.q: ペットの猫が、そこは俺の座る場所だと（ ）ばかりに大声で鳴いている。
items.qr: Petto no neko ga, soko wa ore no suwaru basho da to (___) bakari ni oogoe de naite iru.
items.en: Our pet cat is meowing loudly as if to say "That is my seat!"

opts.en: (as if) to say — classical ん form

items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: The fixed pattern is 「Aと（言わん）ばかりにB」 = "B as if to say A" (point 1); the cat is not really speaking. Only the old negative-volitional 言わん fits before ばかりに here; 言う／言った／言って + ばかりに are not this pattern. (distractor notes added, not in book)

items.q: 自分が利益を（ ）がために、多くの人を犠牲にするなんて許されない。
items.qr: Jibun ga rieki o (___) ga tame ni, ooku no hito o gisei ni suru nante yurusarenai.
items.en: Sacrificing many people just so that you yourself can profit is unforgivable.

opts.en: (in order) to gain — ない-stem + ん

items.why: Answer 1 (book key). Why: 「Aんがために、B」 takes the ない-form stem of the verb: 得(ない) → 得んがために (point 2). The book warns that する becomes せんがために. 得よう／得る／得ない cannot attach to んがために — on their own they would need plain ために (得るために).

items.q: 長年続けてきたバレーボールだが、次の大会（ ）、引退するつもりだ。
items.qr: Naganen tsuzukete kita bareebooru da ga, tsugi no taikai (___), intai suru tsumori da.
items.en: I have played volleyball for many years, but I plan to retire after the next tournament.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: 次の大会 is the last event before 引退 → 「Aを限りに」 = "with A as the last" (point 3). From the book's 解説: 1 だけに = "because A, all the more B"; 2 あげく needs a た-form (Aたあげく) and a bad outcome; 4 にあたって = "now that the time for A has come" — none marks the final occasion.

items.q: アメリカには4日間だけ滞在する予定だったが、ハリケーンの影響で日程の変更を（ ）。
items.qr: Amerika ni wa yokkakan dake taizai suru yotei datta ga, harikeen no eikyou de nittei no henkou o (___).
items.en: I planned to stay in America for only four days, but because of the hurricane I was forced to change my schedule.

opts.en: no room for, out of the question

items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: The hurricane (outside cause) made a schedule change unavoidable → 「Aを余儀なくされる」 (point 4). From the 解説: 1 恐れがある = possibility of something bad (it already happened here, and を doesn't fit — it needs の); 3 禁じえない is for feelings (涙／同情を禁じえない); 4 どころではない = "no room for A" — 変更どころではない makes no sense.

items.q: 経済的に豊かな国に住む人々は、豊かな国（ ）の悩みや苦しみを抱えているものだ。
items.qr: Keizaiteki ni yutaka na kuni ni sumu hitobito wa, yutaka na kuni (___) no nayami ya kurushimi o kakaete iru mono da.
items.en: People who live in economically rich countries have worries and hardships that come precisely from living in a rich country.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why: 「AゆえのB」 = "B caused by A", noun + ゆえの + noun (point 5): worries that come from being a rich country. The 解説 notes 2 しだい is used as 「AはBしだいだ」 (A depends on B). 1 豊かな国ばかりの = "consisting only of rich countries"; 3 ため needs の before it (豊かな国のための) and would mean "for rich countries". (1 and 3 added, not in book)

items.q: もっと早くから取りかかれば、締め切りに間に合った（ ）。
items.qr: Motto hayaku kara torikakareba, shimekiri ni ma ni atta (___).
items.en: If only I had started earlier, I would have made the deadline.

opts.en: as if I would ~! / I will never

items.why: Answer 1 (book key). Why: ば-condition + た-form + 「ものを」 = "if only A, B would have happened (but it didn't)" (point 6) — regret at not starting earlier. From the 解説: 2 ことか = 「どれぐらいA（した）ことか」 (how much!); 3 ものか = "I will (absolutely) never A". 4 ことに goes at the start (残念なことに…) and cannot end a sentence. (4 added, not in book)

items.q: 弟は親の心配をよそに（ ）。
items.qr: Otouto wa oya no shinpai o yoso ni (___).
items.en: Paying no attention to our parents' worry, my younger brother does nothing but play without studying.

opts.t: 勉強もせずに遊んでばかりいる
opts.r: benkyou mo sezu ni asonde bakari iru
opts.en: does nothing but play without studying

opts.t: 不安で寝られなくなってしまった

items.why: Answer 1 (book key). Why: 「AをよそにB」 = "ignoring A, does B" (point 7): B must be the brother's own action that disregards the parents' worry — playing instead of studying. 2 would mean he shares the worry; 3 is what the parents want, not ignoring them; 4 is passive — something done to him, not a choice he makes. (added, not in book)

items.q: 次の委員長だが、山下君をおいて（ ）。
items.qr: Tsugi no iinchou da ga, Yamashita-kun o oite (___).
items.en: As for the next committee chair, there is probably nobody but Yamashita.

opts.t: ほかの人を選んだほうがいい
opts.r: hoka no hito o eranda hou ga ii
opts.en: it is better to choose someone else
there is probably no one else

opts.t: （scan too faint — partly illegible, appears to end in 〜でもよかった）
杉村君にしてはどうだろうか
opts.r: Sugimura-kun ni shite wa dou darou ka

items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: 「AをおいてBない」 = "there is no B other than A" (point 8) — the pattern must close with a negative. Only ほかにいないだろう does. 1 and 4 recommend a different person, which is the opposite of をおいて; 3 is too faint in the scan to read fully, but it is not a negative "nobody else" ending either. (added, not in book)

items.q: 子ども（ ）、同じことを何度も注意させないでください。
items.qr: Kodomo (___), onaji koto o nando mo chuui sasenai de kudasai.
items.en: You're not a child, so please don't make me warn you about the same thing again and again.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: "You're not a child, so…" + a complaint (〜させないでください) = 「Aではあるまいし、B」 (point 1). The 解説 notes たりとも needs a tiny quantity (一円たりとも). とともに and につれて (change in step) make no sense with 子ども here. (3–4 added, not in book)

items.q: 親になる（ ）、親の子どもへの愛情の深さを知るのは難しい。
items.qr: Oya ni naru (___), oya no kodomo e no aijou no fukasa o shiru no wa muzukashii.
items.en: Without becoming a parent yourself, it is hard to know how deep a parent's love for a child is.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why: "Without A, B is difficult" — B is negative (難しい), so 「（こと）なしに」 fits (point 2). The 解説 points out からには = "since A, of course B (must / will)", which would need a positive duty, not 難しい. ばかりに (bad result caused by A) and くらい do not express "without". (1, 3 added, not in book)

items.q: 故郷からたくさんりんごが送られてきたから、あげた（ ）、山田さんに特別な思いがあるわけではない。
items.qr: Kokyou kara takusan ringo ga okurarete kita kara, ageta (___), Yamada-san ni tokubetsu na omoi ga aru wake de wa nai.
items.en: I only gave Yamada some because lots of apples were sent from my hometown — it's not that I have special feelings for her.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: "I only gave them — nothing special about it" = V-た + 「までだ」 (point 3), here in the connecting form までで. The 解説: とたん = "the instant A, (surprising) B"; といっても = "although A, B". せいで blames a cause for a bad result. (4 added, not in book)

items.q: 最近いいこと（ ）、幸せだ。
items.qr: Saikin ii koto (___), shiawase da.
items.en: Lately it's been nothing but good things, so I'm happy.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: いいことずくめ is a set phrase = "nothing but good things" (point 4). From the 解説: のみならず = "not only A but also B" (needs a B); までもない follows a verb (言うまでもなく); まみれ is for dirt/liquids stuck on a surface (血・泥・汗まみれ).

items.q: 言葉の通じない海外での一人暮らしが、いかに大変かは想像に（ ）。
items.qr: Kotoba no tsuujinai kaigai de no hitorigurashi ga, ika ni taihen ka wa souzou ni (___).
items.en: It is easy to imagine how hard it is to live alone abroad where you can't make yourself understood.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key). Why: 想像にかたくない is a fixed phrase = "easy to imagine" (point 5). The 解説: あたらない = 「（辞書形）に（は）あたらない」 "not worth ~ing" (驚くにはあたらない); かかわる = 「Nにかかわる」 "affects / concerns". ちがいない attaches directly to a plain form (大変にちがいない), not to 想像に. (4 added, not in book)

items.q: 夫は私に何の相談もなく仕事をやめ、最近では生活費にまで手をつける（ ）だ。
items.qr: Otto wa watashi ni nan no soudan mo naku shigoto o yame, saikin de wa seikatsuhi ni made te o tsukeru (___) da.
items.en: My husband quit his job without consulting me at all, and lately he has even started dipping into our living expenses.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why: A chain of bad acts (quit without asking → now even the living money) ending in the worst one = 「Aしまつだ」 (point 6). The 解説: きらい is 「Aきらいがある」 "has a tendency to A" — it needs がある, not だ. きっかけ and かわり don't express the final bad outcome. (1–2 added, not in book)

items.q: お忙しい（ ）おいでくださいまして、誠にありがとうございます。
items.qr: Oisogashii (___) oide kudasaimashite, makoto ni arigatou gozaimasu.
items.en: Thank you very much for coming despite being so busy.

opts.en: (though you are) in the middle of

items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why: お忙しいところを + thanks is a fixed polite formula = 「AところをB」 (point 7): "although you are in a busy situation, you kindly came". せいで blames; うちに means "while it is still ~"; にかかわらず follows contrasting pairs or nouns (晴雨にかかわらず), not お忙しい. (added, not in book)

items.q: アルバイト先の店長と（ ）、店員に働かせるばかりで自分は何もしようとしない。
items.qr: Arubaito saki no tenchou to (___), ten'in ni hatarakaseru bakari de jibun wa nani mo shiyou to shinai.
items.en: The manager at my part-time job, honestly — he just makes the staff work and won't do anything himself.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: The rest of the sentence is a complaint about the manager → 「Aときたら、B」 (point 8). といったら mainly heads an exclamation about degree (その美しさといったら…); としたら is a hypothesis; とみたら is not used as a topic marker for criticism. (added, not in book)

items.q: 父は他人の子（ ）、悪いことをしたら、厳しくしかるべきだと考えている。
items.qr: Chichi wa tanin no ko (___), warui koto o shitara, kibishiku shikaru beki da to kangaete iru.
items.en: My father thinks that even if it is someone else's child, you should scold them strictly when they do something bad.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key). Why: "Even if it's someone else's child, (the rule still applies)" = 「Aであれ、B」 (point 1). The 解説: にしては = "for A, B (contrary to expectation)". にとって states a viewpoint; のせいで blames a cause — neither is a concession. (3–4 added, not in book)

items.q: 散歩（ ）、新しくできた本屋をのぞいてくるよ。
items.qr: Sanpo (___), atarashiku dekita honya o nozoite kuru yo.
items.en: I'll go for a walk and take a peek at the new bookshop while I'm at it.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: A walk with a side purpose (peek into the bookshop) = 「Aがてら、B」 (point 2), which attaches directly to a noun like 散歩. ながら needs a verb stem; のおかげで gives a reason; the 解説 notes といっても = "although A, B". (1–2 added, not in book)

items.q: 観光を売りにした町だというのに、平日（ ）、連休にもほとんど観光客がいない。
items.qr: Kankou o uri ni shita machi da to iu no ni, heijitsu (___), renkyuu ni mo hotondo kankoukyaku ga inai.
items.en: Although the town promotes itself on tourism, there are hardly any tourists even on long weekends, let alone on weekdays.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: 平日 (easy case) → 連休にも (harder case) …いない = 「AはおろかB（も）」 (point 3). The 解説: たりとも needs a minimal quantity (一日たりとも). ばかりに and として don't create the "A, and even B" scale. (1, 4 added, not in book)

items.q: 友人と5時に待ち合わせをしていたのだが、子どもに泣かれて、（ ）にも出かけられなかった。
items.qr: Yuujin to goji ni machiawase o shite ita no da ga, kodomo ni nakarete, (___) ni mo dekakerarenakatta.
items.en: I had arranged to meet a friend at five, but my child started crying and I couldn't go out even though I wanted to.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: 「AうにもBない」 = "want to A but can't" takes the volitional form before にも (point 4): 出かけようにも出かけられない. The dictionary form is used only in the variant without も (帰るに帰れない); た-form and potential form never precede にも here.

items.q: 明らかにこちらのミスなのだから、謝罪せず（ ）だろう。
items.qr: Akiraka ni kochira no misu na no da kara, shazai sezu (___) darou.
items.en: Since it is clearly our mistake, we won't get away without apologising.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: せず + にはすまない = 「Aずにはすまない」 "can't get away without apologising" (point 5); the situation (our obvious mistake) makes it unavoidable. The 解説: ほかない = 「（辞書形）ほかない」 — it needs 謝罪する, not せず; the same applies to しかない. ちがいない follows a plain form. (2, 4 added, not in book)

items.q: 父は毎朝トイレのドアを開け（ ）出かける。
items.qr: Chichi wa maiasa toire no doa o ake (___) dekakeru.
items.en: Every morning my father goes out leaving the toilet door open.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: 開け (ます-stem) + 「っぱなし」 = "leave it open" (point 6). まま would need 開けたまま; the 解説 notes かけ is 「V-ます かけ ＋ の ＋ N」 (half-done) and can't be followed by 出かける directly. ながら would mean he opens the door while going out. (1, 3 added, not in book)

items.q: 試験はいよいよ明日だ。今できるのはただ自分を信じること（ ）。
items.qr: Shiken wa iyoiyo ashita da. Ima dekiru no wa tada jibun o shinjiru koto (___).
items.en: The exam is finally tomorrow. All I can do now is simply believe in myself.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key). Why: ただ … のみだ = "only / nothing but" (point 7); ただ in the sentence is the signal. The 解説: までもない follows a dictionary-form verb (言うまでもない). だらけ (covered in, too many bad things) and がち (tends to) don't fit after こと. (2–3 added, not in book)

items.q: クラス委員長に選ばれた坂下君はだれに（ ）責任感が強い生徒だ。
items.qr: Kurasu iinchou ni erabareta Sakashita-kun wa dare ni (___) sekininkan ga tsuyoi seito da.
items.en: Sakashita, who was chosen as class representative, is a student with a stronger sense of responsibility than anyone.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: だれにもまして = "more than anyone" (point 8), comparing his sense of responsibility with everyone else's. The 解説: にもかかわらず = "although A, B"; にしても = "A is understandable, but B (too…)". にとっても has no comparison. (1 added, not in book)

items.q: 頼りにしていた先輩が次々と部をやめてしまい、心細い（ ）。
items.qr: Tayori ni shite ita senpai ga tsugitsugi to bu o yamete shimai, kokorobosoi (___).
items.en: The seniors I relied on have quit the club one after another, and I feel very insecure.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key). Why: A feeling adjective (心細い) + 「かぎりだ」 = "I feel extremely insecure" (point 1). The 解説: 向きだ = 「N1はN2向きだ」 "N1 suits N2". 以上だ and べきだ do not express the speaker's emotion. (2, 4 added, not in book)

items.q: 学生によって差別するなんて、教員に（ ）行為だ。
items.qr: Gakusei ni yotte sabetsu suru nante, kyouin ni (___) koui da.
items.en: Treating students differently depending on who they are is conduct unbecoming of a teacher.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why: Role noun 教員 + に + 「あるまじき」 + 行為 = "conduct a teacher must never commit" (point 2). にすぎない (only, merely) and による (caused by) don't carry the moral criticism; ながらも needs a clause. (added, not in book)

items.q: 今日はこの地区最大のお祭り（ ）、大勢の観光客でにぎわっている。
items.qr: Kyou wa kono chiku saidai no omatsuri (___), oozei no kankoukyaku de nigiwatte iru.
items.en: Since today is the biggest festival in this district, it is bustling with crowds of tourists.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: A special occasion (the biggest festival) → natural result (crowded) = 「Aとあって、B」 (point 3). The 解説: をおいて needs a negative (AをおいてBない); どころか = "not just A but even B". のせいで blames. (3 added, not in book)

items.q: 将来医者になる（ ）、日々努力を重ねている。
items.qr: Shourai isha ni naru (___), hibi doryoku o kasanete iru.
items.en: I am working hard every day in order to become a doctor in the future.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: Purpose + effort = dictionary form + 「べく」 (point 4). The 解説: ところで follows a た-form ("even if A, bad B"); までもなく = "without needing to A". うちに ("while") gives no goal. (2 added, not in book)

items.q: 生徒たちは授業が（ ）や否や、グラウンドに向かっていった。
items.qr: Seitotachi wa jugyou ga (___) ya ina ya, guraundo ni mukatte itta.
items.en: The moment class ended, the students headed for the playground.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: 「Aや否や」 takes the dictionary form (point 5), even though the event is past — the past tense is shown only at the end (向かっていった). 終わった is the trap borrowed from とたん (V-た とたん). (added, not in book)

items.q: 見る（ ）見ていたインターネットに、母校のニュースが出ていた。
items.qr: Miru (___) mite ita intaanetto ni, bokou no nyuusu ga dete ita.
items.en: On the internet I was idly browsing, there was news about my old school.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: The same verb twice (見る…見ていた) with "not really intending" = 「AともなくB」 (point 6). The 解説: なしに attaches to nouns ("without A"); そばから = "as soon as A, (B again and again)". (4 added, not in book)

items.q: 大企業の社長たるもの、（ ）。
items.qr: Daikigyou no shachou taru mono, (___).
items.en: The president of a big company should also think about contributing to the local community.

opts.t: 高級住宅街に住んでいる
opts.en: lives in an exclusive residential area

opts.t: 地域への貢献も考えるべきだ
opts.r: chiiki e no kouken mo kangaeru beki da
opts.en: should also think about contributing to the community

opts.t: 社員から尊敬を集めている
opts.r: shain kara sonkei o atsumete iru

opts.t: 大変な発言力を持っている
opts.r: taihen na hatsugenryoku o motte iru

items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: 「Aたるもの、B」 needs B = what the role requires (はず／べき／てはならない) (point 7). Only option 2 ends in べきだ; 1, 3 and 4 only describe facts. (added, not in book)

items.q: この町に引っ越してきてからというもの、（ ）。
items.qr: Kono machi ni hikkoshite kite kara to iu mono, (___).
items.en: Ever since I moved to this town, I have stopped going out.

opts.t: いろいろ観光名所を回りたい
opts.en: I want to visit various sights

opts.t: 外に出なくなってしまった
早く新しい生活に慣れたい
opts.en: I want to get used to my new life soon

items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: 「Aてからというもの、B」 needs B = a changed state that has lasted since A (point 8). 外に出なくなってしまった is such a change. Wishes (1, 4) and a one-off event (2) cannot follow. (added, not in book)

items.q: 彼のスピーチは高い語学力（ ）、考えの深さに光るものがあった。
items.qr: Kare no supiichi wa takai gogakuryoku (___), kangae no fukasa ni hikaru mono ga atta.
items.en: His speech showed high language skills, of course, but the depth of his thinking really shone.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why: Two strengths, with the stress on the second (考えの深さ) = 「Aもさることながら、B」 (point 1). The 解説: ゆえ = "because of A" (cause), which makes no sense here. さえ and ばかりに don't add a second, bigger merit. (2–3 added, not in book)

items.q: 救急車は命に（ ）病気やけがのときに利用するものだ。
items.qr: Kyuukyuusha wa inochi ni (___) byouki ya kega no toki ni riyou suru mono da.
items.en: An ambulance is something you use for life-threatening illness or injury.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why: 命にかかわる = "life-threatening" (point 2), modifying 病気やけが. The 解説: 足る = 「Aに足るB」 "B worthy of A" (尊敬に足る人) — 命に足る is meaningless. わたる needs a range (長期間にわたる). (2–3 added, not in book)

items.q: 彼女に会った（ ）、少なくとも30分は話に付き合わされることになる。
items.qr: Kanojo ni atta (___), sukunaku tomo sanjuppun wa hanashi ni tsukiawasareru koto ni naru.
items.en: Once you run into her, you end up being made to listen to her for at least thirty minutes.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: "Once you meet her, an unwanted result follows (30 minutes of talk)" = V-た + 「が最後」 (point 3). だけあって praises; ところ reports a discovery; かけて needs 〜から〜にかけて. (added, not in book)

items.q: 一般的に自分と気が合う部下に対する評価は、甘くなる（ ）がある。
items.qr: Ippanteki ni jibun to ki ga au buka ni taisuru hyouka wa, amaku naru (___) ga aru.
items.en: In general, evaluations of subordinates you get along with tend to be lenient.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: 辞書形 + 「きらいがある」 = "has an (undesirable) tendency to" (point 4); being lenient with favourites is such a tendency. きっかけ／かわり make no sense after 甘くなる; こそ cannot be followed by がある here. (added, not in book)

items.q: 結婚して新たな旅立ちをした二人が、幸せになることを願って（ ）。
items.qr: Kekkon shite arata na tabidachi o shita futari ga, shiawase ni naru koto o negatte (___).
items.en: I sincerely wish the two of you, who have married and set out on a new journey, every happiness.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: 願ってやまない = "wish from the heart, continually" (point 5) — the formal phrase for a wedding speech. てしょうがない／てたまらない describe an uncontrollable (often physical) feeling and are casual; ちがいない never follows a て-form. (added, not in book)

items.q: 給料が上がったから、余裕があるとは言えない（ ）、それなりの生活は送れている。
items.qr: Kyuuryou ga agatta kara, yoyuu ga aru to wa ienai (___), sore nari no seikatsu wa okurete iru.
items.en: My salary went up, so although I can't say I'm well off, I can live a reasonable life.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: 〜ないまでも = "not as far as A, but at least B" (point 6): not "well-off", but "a decent life". The 解説: ことはないが follows a ない-form verb (〜ないことはないが) and means "to some degree A, but (a problem)"; ばかりか = "not only A, also B". (3 added, not in book)

items.q: 締め切りを1週間延ばしてもらったところで、（ ）。
items.qr: Shimekiri o isshuukan nobashite moratta tokoro de, (___).
items.en: Even if they extend the deadline by a week, I don't think I'll make it.

opts.t: あと1週間延ばしてもらおう
間に合うとは思えない
opts.r: ma ni au to wa omoenai
opts.en: I don't think I'll make it

opts.t: 一生懸命仕上げようと思う
opts.en: I'll do my best to finish

items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: 「Aたところで、B」 needs a negative / futile B (point 7). 間に合うとは思えない is exactly that. 1 and 3 are intentions and 4 is a positive result — all incompatible. (added, not in book)

items.q: 親といえども、（ ）。
items.qr: Oya to iedomo, (___).
items.en: Even parents can't be said to understand everything about their children.

opts.t: 子どもの教育に熱心であるべきだ
opts.r: kodomo no kyouiku ni nesshin de aru beki da
opts.en: should be keen on their children's education

opts.t: 将来子どもが面倒を見るべきだ
opts.r: shourai kodomo ga mendou o miru beki da
opts.en: children should look after them in future

opts.t: 子どものことを何でも知っている
opts.r: kodomo no koto o nan demo shitte iru

opts.t: 子どもを全部理解しているとは言えない
opts.r: kodomo o zenbu rikai shite iru to wa ienai
opts.en: can't be said to understand their children fully

items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why: 「Aといえども、B」 = "even A (whom you'd expect to…), B (not so)" (point 8). Only 4 contradicts the expectation; 3 simply confirms it, and 1, 2 are statements of duty unrelated to "even". (added, not in book)

items.q: プレゼントは何か残るものをあげたいと思う。食べ物は食べてしまえば（ ）だからだ。
items.qr: Purezento wa nani ka nokoru mono o agetai to omou. Tabemono wa tabete shimaeba (___) da kara da.
items.en: I want to give a present that lasts, because food is gone once it's eaten.

opts.en: as long as / to that extent

items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why: 「Aばそれまで」 = "once A, it's all over" (point 1): food disappears once eaten, unlike a lasting present. The other three don't express "nothing remains". (added, not in book)

items.q: 今回クラスで起きた出来事はわざわざ会議で取り上げる（ ）だろう。
items.qr: Konkai kurasu de okita dekigoto wa wazawaza kaigi de toriageru (___) darou.
items.en: There's probably no need to go out of our way to raise this class incident at a meeting.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why: わざわざ + 辞書形 + 「までもない」 = "no need to go to the trouble of A" (point 2). 足らない and すぎない need に before them (取り上げるに足らない would mean "not worth raising" — close, but the に is missing); かねない warns of a bad possibility. (added, not in book)

items.q: 高田選手は逆風を（ ）、大会新記録で42.195キロを走り切った。
items.qr: Takada senshu wa gyakufuu o (___), taikai shinkiroku de yonjuuni-ten-ichikyuugo kiro o hashirikitta.
items.en: Undaunted by the headwind, Takada ran the full 42.195 km in a new race record.

opts.en: (をもって) with ~ (as the end) / by means of

items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: An obstacle (逆風) overcome with an admirable result = 「Aをものともせずに」 (point 3). The 解説: をもって = "with A (a date) as the last"; をもとにして = "using A as a basis". もちろんのこと (〜はもちろんのこと) doesn't follow を. (4 added, not in book)

items.q: 20年以上勤務した会社をやめさせられることも、今の景気の悪さを考えれば、驚くに（ ）。
items.qr: Nijuunen ijou kinmu shita kaisha o yamesaserareru koto mo, ima no keiki no warusa o kangaereba, odoroku ni (___).
items.en: Considering how bad the economy is now, even being forced out of a company you worked at for over 20 years is nothing to be surprised about.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: 驚くにあたらない = "nothing to be surprised about" (point 4), given the bad economy. The 解説: かたくない is 「（想像／察する）にかたくない」 — "easy to imagine", not used with 驚く. 驚くにちがいない would contradict 考えれば; すぎない follows nouns. (1–2 added, not in book)

items.q: 次の日曜日に田中君も一緒に映画に行く（ ）、予想していなかった。
items.qr: Tsugi no nichiyoubi ni Tanaka-kun mo issho ni eiga ni iku (___), yosou shite inakatta.
items.en: I hadn't expected that Tanaka would come to the film with us next Sunday too.

opts.en: (AといいBといい) both A and B

items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why: 普通形 + 「とは」 + surprise (予想していなかった) (point 5). The 解説: といい needs the pair AといいBといい. といえば changes topic; としても is a concession. (1, 3 added, not in book)

items.q: お風呂のお湯が（ ）ばかりになっていたよ。
items.qr: Ofuro no oyu ga (___) bakari ni natte ita yo.
items.en: The bath water was right on the point of overflowing.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: ない-stem + 「んばかり」 = "on the verge of A" (point 6): the water hasn't overflowed yet. あふれる／あふれた／あふれて + ばかり would mean "only / just overflowed". (added, not in book)

items.q: この問題はクラスで最も成績のよい木下君にして、（ ）。
items.qr: Kono mondai wa kurasu de mottomo seiseki no yoi Kinoshita-kun ni shite, (___).
items.en: Even Kinoshita, the top student in the class, couldn't answer this question.

opts.t: 解けないはずはないだろう
opts.en: surely he can't fail to solve it
I want him to solve it
couldn't come up with the answer

items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: 「Aにして、B」 meaning ① "even A (top level) → bad result" (point 7). 答えが出せなかった is that bad result. Requests (2, 4) don't fit, and 1 is a guess, not a result. (added, not in book)

items.q: 給料が少ないので、100円たりとも、（ ）。
items.qr: Kyuuryou ga sukunai node, hyakuen tari tomo, (___).
items.en: My salary is low, so I can't waste even 100 yen.

opts.t: 上げてくれたらうれしい
opts.en: I'd be happy if they raised it

items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: 「Aたりとも、B」: minimal quantity + negative B (point 8) — 無駄にはできない is the book's own model ending. The other options are positive wishes. (added, not in book)

items.q: 深刻な顔で現れたから、何か悩みがあるのだと（ ）、結婚の報告だった。
items.qr: Shinkoku na kao de arawareta kara, nani ka nayami ga aru no da to (___), kekkon no houkoku datta.
items.en: He turned up looking serious, so I thought he had some worry — but he came to announce his marriage.

opts.en: (と同時に) at the same time as
(とばかりに) as if to say

items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why: Expectation (some worry) → surprising reality (marriage news) = 「Aと思いきや、B」 (point 1). The 解説: ばかりに here would be 「Aと（言わん）ばかりに」 "as if about to say A", which describes behaviour, not a reversed expectation. としたら and と同時に don't give a contrast. (1, 3 added, not in book)

items.q: 合唱クラブの発表会に出かけたが、聞くに（ ）内容だった。
items.qr: Gasshou kurabu no happyoukai ni dekaketa ga, kiku ni (___) naiyou datta.
items.en: I went to the choir club's concert, but it was unbearable to listen to.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: 聞く + 「にたえない」 = "too bad to listen to" (point 2), and the が ("I went, but…") signals disappointment. The 解説: ほかならない = 「Nにほかならない」 "is nothing other than N" — needs a noun. すぎない also follows a noun; 関する makes no sense after 聞くに. (1, 4 added, not in book)

items.q: 5歳（ ）、周りの言うことをすぐ覚えるから、子どもの前では悪い言葉などを使わないようにしている。
items.qr: Gosai (___), mawari no iu koto o sugu oboeru kara, kodomo no mae de wa warui kotoba nado o tsukawanai you ni shite iru.
items.en: By the age of five, children quickly pick up what people around them say, so I try not to use bad words in front of my child.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key). Why: Reaching an age (5歳) where a new characteristic appears = 「Aともなると」 (point 3). The 解説: にしてみれば = "from the point of view of A" (5歳にしてみれば would describe the child's feelings, not a stage). というより and どころか don't fit. (3–4 added, not in book)

items.q: 必ずしも子どもが大人より文章が下手なわけではない。大人にはない、子ども（ ）発想があるからだ。
items.qr: Kanarazushimo kodomo ga otona yori bunshou ga heta na wake de wa nai. Otona ni wa nai, kodomo (___) hassou ga aru kara da.
items.en: Children are not necessarily worse writers than adults, because they have ideas only children have, which adults lack.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: "Ideas adults don't have = ideas only children have" → 「AならではのB」 (point 4). The 解説: めいた = "like A" (子どもめいた = childish-looking — a criticism, not uniqueness). に対する (towards) and さえ (even) don't fit before 発想. (2, 4 added, not in book)

items.q: 部長は君に期待すれば（ ）、厳しくしているんだと思うよ。
items.qr: Buchou wa kimi ni kitai sureba (___), kibishiku shite iru n da to omou yo.
items.en: I think the manager is strict with you precisely because he has high hopes for you.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key). Why: ば-form + 「こそ」 stresses the reason: "precisely because he expects much of you" (point 5) — explaining why he is strict. ほど needs すればするほど; なり and ばかり don't combine with ば like this. (added, not in book)

items.q: この映画はただ若者（ ）、子どもやお年寄りまで楽しめる内容だ。
items.qr: Kono eiga wa tada wakamono (___), kodomo ya otoshiyori made tanoshimeru naiyou da.
items.en: This film can be enjoyed not only by young people but even by children and the elderly.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why: ただ + N + 「のみならず」, then まで in B = "not only young people but even children and the elderly" (point 6). The others don't create "not only A, also B", and none pairs with ただ. (added, not in book)

items.q: 成績優秀な兄にひきかえ、（ ）。
items.qr: Seiseki yuushuu na ani ni hikikae, (___).
items.en: In contrast to her brilliant older brother, the younger sister is no good at studying at all.

opts.t: 弟はうらやましがっている
両親は誇りに思っている
opts.r: ryoushin wa hokori ni omotte iru

opts.t: 一流大学を目指している
opts.en: is aiming for a top university

opts.t: 妹は全く勉強ができない
opts.r: imouto wa mattaku benkyou ga dekinai
opts.en: the younger sister can't study at all

items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why: 「Aにひきかえ、B」 needs B = a different subject with the opposite quality (point 7). Only 妹は全く勉強ができない contrasts with 成績優秀な兄. 1 and 2 are reactions to the brother, 3 is about the brother himself. (added, not in book)

items.q: 友達が引っ越しを手伝ってくれるとはいえ、（ ）。
items.qr: Tomodachi ga hikkoshi o tetsudatte kureru to wa ie, (___).
items.en: Even though my friends will help me move, it will probably take quite a while.

opts.t: かなり時間がかかるだろう
opts.en: it will probably take quite a while

opts.t: 半分の時間で済むのではないか
opts.r: hanbun no jikan de sumu no de wa nai ka
opts.en: maybe it will take half the time

items.why: Answer 1 (book key). Why: 「Aとはいえ、B」 = "true, A, but B" — B must go against what A suggests (point 8). Help from friends suggests it'll be quick; かなり時間がかかるだろう contradicts that. 2 and 4 follow naturally from A; 3 is an intention. (added, not in book)

items.q: 老人の方もやはり誰かに（ 1 ）、何やかや要求する。
items.qr: Roujin no hou mo yahari dare ka ni ( 1 ), naniyakaya youkyuu suru.
items.en: The elderly people, too, want to lean on someone after all, so they ask for all sorts of things.

opts.t: 甘えてみたいものだから
opts.en: because they want to lean on (someone)
if they want to lean on

items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.176). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): the volunteer is very kind → the residents, wanting to lean on someone, → make all kinds of demands. A reason clause is needed, so 〜たいものだから. Conditions (2, 4) don't fit a general fact, and 3 (past "tried") doesn't explain a habitual demand.

items.q: これは確かに素晴らしいことである。（ 2 ）、このような行為を、この人は無償でやっているのだから、ますますそれは「善行」と言うべきである。
items.qr: Kore wa tashika ni subarashii koto de aru. ( 2 ), kono you na koui o, kono hito wa mushou de yatte iru no da kara, masumasu sore wa "zenkou" to iu beki de aru.
items.en: This is certainly wonderful. What's more, this person does it for nothing, so all the more it should be called a "good deed".
items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): the residents become happy and do things they normally can't → not stopping at that (= しかも) → it is done for free. ますます ("all the more") confirms an added point. したがって gives a result, ところで changes topic, なぜなら would need 〜からだ.

items.q: しかし、こんな人が時たま来てくれると、施設の人たちが後で（ 3 ）。
items.qr: Shikashi, konna hito ga tokitama kite kureru to, shisetsu no hitotachi ga ato de ( 3 ).
items.en: But when such a person comes now and then, the staff of the home end up having a hard time afterwards.

opts.en: end up having a hard time
will they have a hard time?

items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): the next sentence says residents who have tasted being pampered stop doing things themselves and depend on others — as a result the staff end up struggling (〜ことになる). 1 is causative and the staff are not the cause; 2 (permission) and 4 (doubt) don't state the consequence.

items.q: 施設にいる人たちは、それにいちいち応じて居られないし、やはり老人と言っても出来る限りは自立的に（ 4 ）。
items.qr: Shisetsu ni iru hitotachi wa, sore ni ichiichi oujite irarenai shi, yahari roujin to itte mo dekiru kagiri wa jiritsuteki ni ( 4 ).
items.en: The staff can't respond to every single request, and besides, even if they are old, one would like them to live as independently as they can.

opts.en: one would like them to live

items.why: Answer 1 (book key). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): 老人と言っても = "it's true they are old, but" → a wish from the staff's side follows: as far as possible they would like them to live independently (〜て欲しいものだ). 2 and 4 describe facts, 3 is casual advice — none expresses the staff's hope.

items.q: 時には、この老人が、ボランティアの誰それさんは（ 5 ）、ここの施設の人は冷たい人ばかりだ、などと言いだすかもしれない。
items.qr: Toki ni wa, kono roujin ga, borantia no dare sore-san wa ( 5 ), koko no shisetsu no hito wa tsumetai hito bakari da, nado to iidasu kamo shirenai.
items.en: Sometimes the resident might even start saying, "Volunteer so-and-so is a kind person, but the staff here are all cold."
items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): the next sentence says this makes the staff unhappy, so the remark must praise the volunteer and criticise the staff — 優しい人だけど sets up exactly that contrast. 1 and 3 are conditions; 2 would call the volunteer cold too.

items.q: けれども、ほんとうに一緒に考えているだけだったら、先生としてちょっと（ 1 ）。
items.qr: Keredomo, hontou ni issho ni kangaete iru dake dattara, sensei to shite chotto ( 1 ).
items.en: However, if the teacher really only thinks alongside the students, that's a bit too unreliable for a teacher.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.178). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): the previous sentence says thinking together is the basic stance, then けれども signals that something different follows — so "only thinking together" is criticised: ちょっと頼りなさすぎる. 1, 2 and 4 are all positive about relying on the teacher.

items.q: 生徒が先生にすごみを（ 2 ）、教師としてはやっていけないものだ。
items.qr: Seito ga sensei ni sugomi o ( 2 ), kyoushi to shite wa yatte ikenai mono da.
items.en: If students don't feel anything impressive in the teacher, he can't get by as a teacher.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): right after comes 教師としてはやっていけない, and its reason is "the moment students think they are equal, they stop listening". So the condition must be "if students don't feel the teacher's すごみ" → 感じないようでは. The other conditions would not lead to a negative result.

items.q: 高圧的に「…」といった感じで言われると、生徒が突き放されたような気になって、（ 3 ）。
items.qr: Kouatsuteki ni "…" to itta kanji de iwareru to, seito ga tsukihanasareta you na ki ni natte, ( 3 ).
items.en: When spoken to in a high-handed way ("…"), students feel pushed away and may well lose their motivation.

opts.t: やる気を起こさせられる
やる気を失いかねない

items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): 突き放されたような気になって ("feeling pushed away") naturally leads to losing motivation → やる気を失いかねない; （ます形）かねない means "there is a possibility of ~". The other three are positive. (The teacher's quoted words are shortened to 「…」 here.)

items.q: だから「これについて一緒に考えてみよう」と、心情的には共感的な立場で向かうべきなのだが、（ 4 ）、というのが望ましい。
items.qr: Dakara "kore ni tsuite issho ni kangaete miyou" to, shinjouteki ni wa kyoukanteki na tachiba de mukau beki na no da ga, ( 4 ), to iu no ga nozomashii.
items.en: So you should approach students sympathetically — "let's think about this together" — but it is best that your preparation is solidly in place.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): …べきなのだが sets up a contrast: while showing the attitude "let's think together", the teacher must have a splendid answer ready that convinces the students → 用意はしっかりある. 1 contradicts this; 2 and 4 put the preparation on someone else.

items.q: 最終的には「ほう」と（ 5 ）だけのものをもって臨む、というのが授業の王道だと思う。
items.qr: Saishuuteki ni wa "hou" to ( 5 ) dake no mono o motte nozomu, to iu no ga jugyou no oudou da to omou.
items.en: In the end, I think the proper way to teach is to come to class with enough to make the students say "Oh, I see!".
items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): the frame is 教師が生徒に「ほう」と言わせる — by showing a splendid answer, the teacher makes the students say "Oh!" (impresses them). The teacher is the causer, so the plain causative 言わせる; 言わせられる would make the teacher the one forced to speak.

items.q: 場がかなりほぐれてきたのに、相変わらず「（ 1 ）」のような感じで態度も口調も硬い人、これなど場の空気が読めない人の典型である。
items.qr: Ba ga kanari hogurete kita no ni, aikawarazu "( 1 )" no you na kanji de taido mo kuchou mo katai hito, kore nado ba no kuuki ga yomenai hito no tenkei de aru.
items.en: Even though the mood has relaxed quite a bit, someone who stays as stiff as a "stone" in attitude and tone — that is a typical person who can't read the room.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.180). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): right after comes 態度も口調も硬い人; the thing we picture as hard is a stone → 石.

items.q: これでは、相手との距離を縮めることなどとうていできない。（ 2 ）、話題がなかなか広がらないので場が盛り上がらず、…
items.qr: Kore de wa, aite to no kyori o chijimeru koto nado toutei dekinai. ( 2 ), wadai ga nakanaka hirogaranai node ba ga moriagarazu, …
items.en: That way you can never close the distance with the other person. Worse than that, the topics don't spread and the gathering never livens up, …
items.why: Answer 1 (book key). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): 「A。それどころか、B」 = "not just A, but B, further along the scale". A = you can't get closer; B = the talk dies and everyone goes silent — a worse result. それにもかかわらず needs a contradiction; それにつれて needs gradual parallel change; それとも offers an alternative in a question.

items.q: 話題がなかなか広がらないので場が盛り上がらず、（ 3 ）誰もが無口になってしまう。
items.qr: Wadai ga nakanaka hirogaranai node ba ga moriagarazu, ( 3 ) daremo ga mukuchi ni natte shimau.
items.en: The topics don't spread, the gathering doesn't liven up, and in the end everyone falls silent.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key). Why (book's 解説): しまいには = 最終的には ("finally"), the last stage of a worsening chain, matched by 〜てしまう. わざわざ and あえて describe intention (nobody chooses to go silent); せいぜい limits a quantity.

items.q: 相手の話を聞かずにひとりでしゃべりまくっているような人（ 4 ）空気を読めない人と言える。
items.qr: Aite no hanashi o kikazu ni hitori de shaberimakutte iru you na hito ( 4 ) kuuki o yomenai hito to ieru.
items.en: Someone who talks on and on alone without listening to others can also be called a person who can't read the room.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): the passage has already named stiff people and people who only ask formulaic questions as those who can't read the room; the non-stop talker is one more example → も ("also"). は would set him in contrast, が would present him as the only one.

items.q: 話のつまらない人というのは、「場の空気を感じる感性が（ 5-a ）人」と言い換えてもいい。感性の（ 5-b ）人なら、場の空気がちょっと白けたと感じたら、自分が三枚目になって場がなごむことを言ってみるだろうし、…
items.qr: Hanashi no tsumaranai hito to iu no wa, "ba no kuuki o kanjiru kansei ga ( 5-a ) hito" to iikaete mo ii. Kansei no ( 5-b ) hito nara, ba no kuuki ga chotto shiraketa to kanjitara, jibun ga sanmaime ni natte ba ga nagomu koto o itte miru darou shi, …
items.en: A boring talker could be described as "a person whose sensitivity to the mood of the room is dull". A person with sharp sensitivity, sensing the mood has gone a little flat, would play the clown and say something to lighten things up, …

opts.t: a 鈍い b 鈍い
a 鈍い b 鋭い
a 鋭い b 鈍い
a 鋭い b 鋭い

items.why: Answer 2 (book key). Why (book's 解説, paraphrased): a describes 話のつまらない人 → 感性が鈍い; b describes someone who adjusts to the mood (cheers up a flat room, holds back in an overheated one) → 感性の鋭い人.

items.q: この池は多くの鳥が羽を（ ）に来ます。
items.qr: Kono ike wa ooku no tori ga hane o (___) ni kimasu.
items.en: Many birds come to this pond to rest their wings.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.22). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 休める is used together with 心, 体, 頭, 羽 and similar words. (added, not in book) 羽を休める is the set phrase for a bird stopping to rest; the 〜に来る pattern needs the masu-stem, so 休め.

items.q: 社員全員が「さん」で呼び合う習慣は、徐々に社内に（ ）いった。
items.qr: Shain zen'in ga "san" de yobiau shuukan wa, jojo ni shanai ni (___) itta.
items.en: The custom of all employees calling each other "-san" gradually spread through the company.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.22). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): In this sentence 広まる means almost the same as 広がる. (added, not in book) A custom, rumour or idea 広まる "spreads among people"; the other three are transitive actions that need a person doing them.

items.q: 横浜は、貿易で（ ）都市である。
items.qr: Yokohama wa, boueki de (___) toshi de aru.
items.en: Yokohama is a city that prospered through trade.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.22). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): さかえる means the same as 繁栄する / 繁盛する (to prosper, thrive).

items.q: この番組は、あまり人気が出なかったので、1カ月で放送が（ ）。
items.qr: Kono bangumi wa, amari ninki ga denakatta node, ikkagetsu de housou ga (___).
items.en: This programme never became very popular, so it was taken off the air after one month.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.22). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Stopping a broadcast partway is called 打ち切る. It is also used with 販売 (sales), 契約 (contract), 会見 (press conference) and similar words.

items.q: 砂浜を歩いていたら穴に足が（ ）しまった。
items.qr: Sunahama o aruite itara ana ni ashi ga (___) shimatta.
items.en: While I was walking on the beach, my foot got stuck in a hole.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.22). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Very close in meaning to 入る. はまる also has the meaning 夢中になる (to get hooked on something).

items.q: 脳は言語や感情を（ ）器官である。
items.qr: Nou wa gengo ya kanjou o (___) kikan de aru.
items.en: The brain is the organ that governs language and emotion.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.22). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Remember it as the phrase 〜をつかさどる器官 (the organ in charge of …).

items.q: このうどんは、材料の小麦の品質に（ ）います。
items.qr: Kono udon wa, zairyou no komugi no hinshitsu ni (___) imasu.
items.en: This udon is particular about the quality of the wheat it is made from.

opts.en: take good care of, be kind to

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.22). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Of the four, only こだわる can be used together with 品質 (quality).

items.q: この薬には痛みを（ ）効果があります。
items.qr: Kono kusuri ni wa itami o (___) kouka ga arimasu.
items.en: This medicine has the effect of easing pain.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.22). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): It means 痛みを軽くする (to make pain lighter).

items.q: この施設に（ ）いる器具はすべて無料で利用できます。
items.qr: Kono shisetsu ni (___) iru kigu wa subete muryou de riyou dekimasu.
items.en: All the equipment this facility is furnished with can be used free of charge.

opts.en: be soaked in (浸かる) / use (使う)

items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.22). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Written in kanji as 備わって. Also remember the related word 設備 (equipment, facilities).

items.q: 彼は部長に仕事における過ちを（ ）。
items.qr: Kare wa buchou ni shigoto ni okeru ayamachi o (___).
items.en: He was reproached by the department head for a mistake he made at work.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.22). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): とがめる is used together with 過ち (error), 失敗 (failure) and similar words. (added, not in book) The passive 〜に〜をとがめられる = "be blamed by someone for something".

items.q: 決まりに（ ）ら、罰を受けなければならない。
items.qr: Kimari ni (___) ra, batsu o ukenakereba naranai.
items.en: If you go against the rules, you have to accept the punishment.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.24). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Work it out from 決まり (rules) and 罰を受ける (be punished). (added, not in book) むかう also takes に (駅に向かう), but only そむく means acting against a rule.

items.q: すり傷がかゆくて（ ）いたら、血が出てしまった。
items.qr: Surikizu ga kayukute (___) itara, chi ga dete shimatta.
items.en: My scrape was itchy and I kept scratching it, and it started to bleed.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.24). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): ひっかく means almost the same as (かゆいところを)かく — to scratch (an itch).

items.q: 7歳のときに、「ピアノがほしい！」と親に（ ）買ってもらいました。
items.qr: Nanasai no toki ni, "Piano ga hoshii!" to oya ni (___) katte moraimashita.
items.en: When I was seven, I begged my parents, "I want a piano!", and they bought me one.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.24). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): It means pushing hard with a request — "please buy me what I want".

items.q: お祭りの間は連日多くの人で（ ）いて、客の流れが途絶えることがなかった。
items.qr: Omatsuri no aida wa renjitsu ooku no hito de (___) ite, kyaku no nagare ga todaeru koto ga nakatta.
items.en: During the festival the place was bustling with crowds every day, and the stream of visitors never stopped.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.24). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): The hints are 多くの人 (many people) and 客の流れが途絶えることがなかった (the flow of visitors never stopped). (added, not in book) The subject is the place (implied), so 〜で にぎわう "be lively with …" fits; さわぐ is what people do, and 多くの人でさわぐ is not natural.

items.q: 彼は陸上の100メートル走の世界記録に（ ）いる。
items.qr: Kare wa rikujou no hyaku meetoru sou no sekai kiroku ni (___) iru.
items.en: He is going after the world record in the 100 m sprint.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.24). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Remember it as the phrase 記録にいどむ (to challenge a record). (added, not in book) うちこむ also takes に (仕事に打ち込む) but means throwing yourself into an activity, not attempting a record.

items.q: スピーチの言葉を間違えて、みんなの前で恥を（ ）しまった。
items.qr: Supiichi no kotoba o machigaete, minna no mae de haji o (___) shimatta.
items.en: I got a word wrong in my speech and embarrassed myself in front of everyone.

opts.en: (恥を)かく — be put to shame

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.24). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Remember it as the phrase 恥をかく (to be embarrassed).

items.q: 歯をみがいた後は、口の中をよく（ ）ください。
items.qr: Ha o migaita ato wa, kuchi no naka o yoku (___) kudasai.
items.en: After brushing your teeth, please rinse your mouth well.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.24). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Remember it as the phrase 口をゆすぐ (to rinse one's mouth).

items.q: 子猫を飼い始めたが、なかなか私に（ ）としない。
items.qr: Koneko o kaihajimeta ga, nakanaka watashi ni (___) to shinai.
items.en: I have started keeping a kitten, but it just won't warm up to me.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.24). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): なつく is said of an animal or child growing fond of its owner or parent. (added, not in book) にげようとしない would mean "it doesn't try to run away" — the opposite of the complaint なかなか…ない sets up.

items.q: 時間がないので今日は朝ご飯をパンと牛乳で（ ）た。
items.qr: Jikan ga nai node kyou wa asagohan o pan to gyuunyuu de (___) ta.
items.en: I had no time, so today I made do with bread and milk for breakfast.

opts.en: let hold; made last (持たせる)

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.24). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Learn the pattern 〜を〜ですます (to make do with … for …).

items.q: 新しい会社に入ったばかりなのに、もう「やめたい」と（ ）いる。
items.qr: Atarashii kaisha ni haitta bakari na noni, mou "yametai" to (___) iru.
items.en: He has only just joined the new company, yet he is already grumbling, "I want to quit."
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.24). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): ぼやく means voicing complaints and dissatisfaction. (added, not in book) Only ぼやく is a verb of saying, so only it can follow a quotation 「…」と.

items.q: 練習中は、走って走って、（ ）走ります。
items.qr: Renshuuchuu wa, hashitte hashitte, (___) hashirimasu.
items.en: In practice we run and run — we just keep on running.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.34). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): It describes continuing the same thing, or repeating only that one thing.

items.q: 一生懸命書いた論文の原稿を、教授に（ ）直された。
items.qr: Isshoukenmei kaita ronbun no genkou o, kyouju ni (___) naosareta.
items.en: The professor corrected every part of the thesis draft I had worked so hard on.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.34). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): ことごとく means すべて (all). It is often used with 断られる (be turned down), 否定される (be denied) and the like. (added, not in book) ちっとも must be followed by a negative (ちっとも直されなかった), so it cannot fit here.

items.q: この問題は高校生にさえ難しいのに、まして中学生には（ ）です。
items.qr: Kono mondai wa koukousei ni sae muzukashii noni, mashite chuugakusei ni wa (___) desu.
items.en: This problem is hard even for high-school students, so it is all the more so for junior-high students.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.34). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): It means "even more 〜 than that" or "increasingly 〜". (added, not in book) Watch the frame: AさえX、ましてBはなおさらX ("even A is X — B, all the more so").

items.q: 物価上昇による運賃改定で、バスも電車も（ ）値上がりした。
items.qr: Bukka joushou ni yoru unchin kaitei de, basu mo densha mo (___) neagari shita.
items.en: With the fare revision caused by rising prices, buses and trains alike all went up.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.34). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): のきなみ means "all in the same way"; it is used as AもBものきなみ〜. (added, not in book) なにとぞ only goes with requests (なにとぞよろしくお願いいたします).

items.q: 前のけんかの反省のせいか、今日の彼は（ ）優しい。
items.qr: Mae no kenka no hansei no sei ka, kyou no kare wa (___) yasashii.
items.en: Maybe because he feels bad about our last fight, he is awfully nice today.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.34). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): やけに means とても, used in the sense "much more than you would think". It also has meanings like むやみに / やたらに (excessively). (added, not in book) ちっとも and さっぱり would need a negative (ちっとも優しくない).

items.q: 自信を持っていた実験が失敗して、彼は（ ）肩を落とした。
items.qr: Jishin o motte ita jikken ga shippai shite, kare wa (___) kata o otoshita.
items.en: The experiment he had been confident about failed, and his shoulders slumped in dejection.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.34). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): It describes strength draining out of you from disappointment. がっくりと肩を落とした is a very common expression.

items.q: 最近すぐ疲れるので、体力がなくなってきたと（ ）思う。
items.qr: Saikin sugu tsukareru node, tairyoku ga nakunatte kita to (___) omou.
items.en: I get tired so quickly these days that I really feel my stamina is going.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.34). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): It means "it was so before as well, but lately (this time) I feel it especially strongly", and is often used with 反省する, 思う, 感じる. The speaker strongly feels the loss of stamina, so つくづく fits best.

items.q: 思ったことを、気ままに、（ ）と、書いていこうと思います。
items.qr: Omotta koto o, kimama ni, (___) to, kaite ikou to omoimasu.
items.en: I plan to write down whatever comes to mind, freely and at a gentle pace.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.34). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): ぼつぼつ means something like ゆっくりと (slowly). As in ぼつぼつ出かけましょうか, it can also mean the same as そろそろ (it's about time).

items.q: 田中さんのアドバイスのおかげで、ホームページも（ ）できました。
items.qr: Tanaka-san no adobaisu no okage de, hoomupeeji mo (___) dekimashita.
items.en: Thanks to Mr Tanaka's advice, the website is mostly finished too.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.34). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): おおかた means roughly だいたい (mostly). In a form like おおかたやめるだろうと思っていた it also means おそらく / 多分 (probably).

items.q: これ以上逃げることはできない。（ ）これまでだ。
items.qr: Kore ijou nigeru koto wa dekinai. (___) kore made da.
items.en: I can't run any further. This is the end now.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.34). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): もはや means もう (already, by now). (added, not in book) もはやこれまでだ is a set expression of giving up ("it is all over").

items.q: 現在、インターネットには（ ）数のブログがある。
items.qr: Genzai, intaanetto ni wa (___) kazu no burogu ga aru.
items.en: There is now an enormous number of blogs on the internet.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.30). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): おびただしい数の〜 means "an extremely large number of …".
items.unit: 文脈規定 イ形容詞

items.q: 3人の中で、会長に（ ）のはだれだと思いますか。
items.qr: Sannin no naka de, kaichou ni (___) no wa dare da to omoimasu ka.
items.en: Of the three, who do you think is fit to be chairperson?
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.30). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Learn it as 〜にふさわしい (suitable for …).
items.unit: 文脈規定 イ形容詞

items.q: 彼女に何を質問しても、「うん」という（ ）返事しかしない。
items.qr: Kanojo ni nani o shitsumon shite mo, "un" to iu (___) henji shika shinai.
items.en: Whatever you ask her, all you get is a curt "Yeah."
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.30). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): A word showing an unfriendly, uninterested manner; finishing a reply with the single word "un" is そっけない. (added, not in book) こころよい返事 would be the opposite — a willing, friendly answer (快く引き受ける).
items.unit: 文脈規定 イ形容詞

items.q: 面接のときは、厳しい質問をされても（ ）顔をしないほうがいい。
items.qr: Mensetsu no toki wa, kibishii shitsumon o sarete mo (___) kao o shinai hou ga ii.
items.en: In an interview, it is best not to pull a sour face even when you get a tough question.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.30). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): しぶい顔 expresses dissatisfaction or perplexity. (added, not in book) しぶとい differs by one kana — the "partly the same form" trap. It describes a person who never gives up, not a face.
items.unit: 文脈規定 イ形容詞

items.q: たき火をすると（ ）目が開けられなくなることがある。
items.qr: Takibi o suru to (___) me ga akerarenaku naru koto ga aru.
items.en: When you have a bonfire, it can get so smoky that you can't keep your eyes open.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.30). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): It describes coughing or watering eyes because of smoke. It also has the meaning "hard to approach, awkward to be around". (added, not in book) まぶしい also stops you opening your eyes, but it is about strong light; たき火 points to smoke.
items.unit: 文脈規定 イ形容詞

items.q: 彼の運転は、急な発進や停止が多く、とても（ ）。
items.qr: Kare no unten wa, kyuu na hasshin ya teishi ga ooku, totemo (___).
items.en: His driving is full of sudden starts and stops — it is very rough.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.30). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 急な発進や停止が多く (many sudden starts and stops) is the hint.
items.unit: 文脈規定 イ形容詞

items.q: 毎日、食後に薬を飲むのは（ ）。
items.qr: Mainichi, shokugo ni kusuri o nomu no wa (___).
items.en: Having to take medicine after meals every day is a bother.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.30). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Here it means 面倒くさい (a hassle); it can also mean 気が重い (depressing to think about).
items.unit: 文脈規定 イ形容詞

items.q: 東の空を見ていたら、（ ）月が上がってきた。
items.qr: Higashi no sora o mite itara, (___) tsuki ga agatte kita.
items.en: As I was watching the eastern sky, a perfectly round moon came up.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.30). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): An emphatic form of まるい: it means a perfect circle.
items.unit: 文脈規定 イ形容詞

items.q: レポートは英語で書いてもよいが、日本語で書くことが（ ）。
items.qr: Repooto wa eigo de kaite mo yoi ga, nihongo de kaku koto ga (___).
items.en: You may write the report in English, but writing it in Japanese is preferable.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.30). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): のぞましい means 好ましい (preferable).
items.unit: 文脈規定 イ形容詞

items.q: 医療技術の（ ）進歩により、死亡率がかなり減少した。
items.qr: Iryou gijutsu no (___) shinpo ni yori, shibouritsu ga kanari genshou shita.
items.en: Thanks to remarkable progress in medical technology, the death rate has fallen considerably.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.30). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): いちじるしい has a meaning like めざましい (remarkable). (added, not in book) The tips page gives this very phrase: 発展・変化がいちじるしい.
items.unit: 文脈規定 イ形容詞

items.q: 子どもたちに、2度とガラスを割らないよう（ ）で注意した。
items.qr: Kodomotachi ni, nido to garasu o waranai you (___) de chuui shita.
items.en: I warned the children verbally never to break the glass again.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.26). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): The で in で注意した is the hint: the question asks how the warning was given, so choose 1. (added, not in book) 厳重 also goes with 注意, but as 厳重に注意する, not 厳重で.

items.q: 彼の病気は今、大変危険な状態にあり、面会（ ）である。
items.qr: Kare no byouki wa ima, taihen kiken na joutai ni ari, menkai (___) de aru.
items.en: His illness is now at a very dangerous stage, and no visitors are allowed.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.26). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Learn it as the set expression 面会謝絶 (visitors refused).

items.q: 彼は明るく活発で仕事ができるので、すべての社員の（ ）となるような存在である。
items.qr: Kare wa akaruku kappatsu de shigoto ga dekiru node, subete no shain no (___) to naru you na sonzai de aru.
items.en: He is cheerful, energetic and good at his job, so he is a model for every employee.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.26). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Same meaning as 手本 (an example to follow). (added, not in book) All four share 模 — exactly the "same kanji" distractor type from the tips page. 模倣 is the act of copying, not the person you copy.

items.q: この公園は丘の上にあるので、とても（ ）がいい。
items.qr: Kono kouen wa oka no ue ni aru node, totemo (___) ga ii.
items.en: This park is on a hill, so it has a wonderful view.

opts.en: (stem of 素晴らしい — not a noun)
scrambled 景色 — not a real word

items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.26). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 見晴らし means being able to see far into the distance. Option 4 would be acceptable if it were 景色 (keshiki, scenery).

items.q: この書類は、あとで（ ）にとじておいてください。
items.qr: Kono shorui wa, ato de (___) ni tojite oite kudasai.
items.en: Please put these papers into a file later.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.26). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Learn it as (紙、書類を) ファイルにとじる — to bind (papers) into a file.

items.q: さらに知りたい情報は、あちらの検索（ ）で調べることもできます。
items.qr: Sara ni shiritai jouhou wa, achira no kensaku (___) de shiraberu koto mo dekimasu.
items.en: If you want more information, you can also look it up at the search corner over there.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.26). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): コーナー has the meaning "one section (of a place)".

items.q: 彼がいつも僕と競争したがるのは、僕のことを（ ）だと思っているからだそうだ。
items.qr: Kare ga itsumo boku to kyousou shitagaru no wa, boku no koto o (___) da to omotte iru kara da sou da.
items.en: Apparently the reason he always wants to compete with me is that he sees me as his rival.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.26). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 競争 (competition) is the hint.

items.q: 山で（ ）した人を助け出すには、ヘリコプターが役に立つ。
items.qr: Yama de (___) shita hito o tasukedasu ni wa, herikoputaa ga yaku ni tatsu.
items.en: Helicopters are useful for rescuing people who have got into trouble in the mountains.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.26). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 助け出す (rescue) is the hint. (added, not in book) 災害 is the disaster itself (地震などの災害); a person does not 災害する.

items.q: このソフトはすべてのOSに（ ）している。
items.qr: Kono sofuto wa subete no OS ni (___) shite iru.
items.en: This software works with every operating system.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.26). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): It originally means "facing each other", and from there it came to mean "usable (with)".

items.q: 警察官に免許証を（ ）するように求められた。
items.qr: Keisatsukan ni menkyoshou o (___) suru you ni motomerareta.
items.en: A police officer asked me to show my driving licence.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.26). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 提示 means taking something out (or bringing it along) and showing it. (added, not in book) 提示 and 指示 share 示 (show) — 指示する means to instruct, which the officer does, not the driver.

items.q: 始める前に、今日の会議の内容の（ ）をお話ししておきます。
items.qr: Hajimeru mae ni, kyou no kaigi no naiyou no (___) o ohanashi shite okimasu.
items.en: Before we start, let me give you an outline of what today's meeting will cover.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.28). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 概要 (gaiyou) has the same meaning.

items.q: 引っ越しの業者に、引っ越し料金の（ ）を出してもらった。
items.qr: Hikkoshi no gyousha ni, hikkoshi ryoukin no (___) o dashite moratta.
items.en: I had the moving company give me an estimate of the moving charges.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.28). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): It means calculating charges or costs in advance; 予算 (budget) is roughly similar. (added, not in book) 見込み shares 見 and also looks ahead, but it is a forecast (合格の見込み), not a price quote.

items.q: 自分の意見を一方的に言うだけでは、相手の（ ）を買うだけだ。
items.qr: Jibun no iken o ippouteki ni iu dake de wa, aite no (___) o kau dake da.
items.en: If you only push your own opinion one-sidedly, you will just turn the other person against you.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.28). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Learn the phrase 反感を買う (to provoke antipathy). (added, not in book) 〜を買う here means "bring on yourself"; 同情 normally goes with 同情する / 同情を集める.

items.q: 老後は、仕事をしないで（ ）のある生活を送りたいと思っている。
items.qr: Rougo wa, shigoto o shinaide (___) no aru seikatsu o okuritai to omotte iru.
items.en: In my old age I want to stop working and live a relaxed life with time to spare.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.28). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 余裕 (yoyuu) has the same meaning.

items.q: 新しい製品の開発のためには、社員の（ ）を重視しています。
items.qr: Atarashii seihin no kaihatsu no tame ni wa, shain no (___) o juushi shite imasu.
items.en: To develop new products, we put great weight on our employees' ideas.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.28). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): It means 考え, 発想 (thinking, ideas).

items.q: 今まで集めた（ ）を一般の人に公開するために、美術館を造った。
items.qr: Ima made atsumeta (___) o ippan no hito ni koukai suru tame ni, bijutsukan o tsukutta.
items.en: A museum was built to open the collection gathered so far to the public.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.28). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): コレクション means "things that have been collected".

items.q: 後から見てもわかるように、ペンで（ ）しておいた。
items.qr: Ato kara mite mo wakaru you ni, pen de (___) shite oita.
items.en: I marked it with a pen so that I would still understand it when I looked later.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.28). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): マークする here means しるしをつける (to put a mark on). (added, not in book) ラベル is a stuck-on tag (ラベルを貼る); ラベルする is not used.

items.q: 友達の家の花びんを割ってしまったので、（ ）しようと思っている。
items.qr: Tomodachi no ie no kabin o watte shimatta node, (___) shiyou to omotte iru.
items.en: I broke a vase at my friend's house, so I intend to pay for it.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.28). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): It means paying for the broken vase or buying the same one again. (added, not in book) 返済 is paying back borrowed money (ローンの返済); 弁償 is paying for damage you caused.

items.q: 緊張のあまり、スピーチの内容を（ ）してしまった。
items.qr: Kinchou no amari, supiichi no naiyou o (___) shite shimatta.
items.en: I was so nervous that what I meant to say in my speech went right out of my head.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.28). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Written 度忘れ; it means forgetting something and being unable to recall it. (added, not in book) だいなし takes 〜をだいなしにする (ruin something), not 〜をだいなしする.

items.q: 地球は約24時間で1回（ ）する。
items.qr: Chikyuu wa yaku nijuuyo jikan de ikkai (___) suru.
items.en: The earth rotates once in about 24 hours.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.28). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Turning by itself is called 自転; it is often used for celestial bodies. (added, not in book) Its partner is 公転 (kouten), revolving around the sun. All four options share 転 — the "same kanji" trap.

items.q: 犬は、人間が感じることのできない（ ）においをかぐことができる。
items.qr: Inu wa, ningen ga kanjiru koto no dekinai (___) nioi o kagu koto ga dekiru.
items.en: Dogs can pick up faint smells that humans cannot sense.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.32). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): かすかな means "very small, weak"; here わずかな would also work.
items.unit: 文脈規定 ナ形容詞

items.q: このアパートは、日当たりが（ ）で、駅からも近いです。
items.qr: Kono apaato wa, hiatari ga (___) de, eki kara mo chikai desu.
items.en: This apartment gets plenty of sunlight and is close to the station too.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.32). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 日当たりが良好 means 日当たりがよい (gets good sunlight). (added, not in book) 新鮮 is a な-adjective too, but it is for food, air or impressions, not sunlight.
items.unit: 文脈規定 ナ形容詞

items.q: このマンションなら、サラリーマンでも（ ）価格で購入できる。
items.qr: Kono manshon nara, sarariiman demo (___) kakaku de kounyuu dekiru.
items.en: With this condominium, even an ordinary salaried worker can buy at an affordable price.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.32). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): てごろな means "just right (for doing something)".
items.unit: 文脈規定 ナ形容詞

items.q: 犯人逮捕の（ ）てがかりが見つからないまま、1カ月が過ぎてしまった。
items.qr: Hannin taiho no (___) tegakari ga mitsukaranai mama, ikkagetsu ga sugite shimatta.
items.en: A month has gone by without any strong lead toward arresting the culprit.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.32). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 有力な expresses having strong power to make something happen (here: to lead to an arrest).
items.unit: 文脈規定 ナ形容詞

items.q: あれこれ言われる前に自分から社長の職を辞めたのは（ ）判断だった。
items.qr: Arekore iwareru mae ni jibun kara shachou no shoku o yameta no wa (___) handan datta.
items.en: Stepping down as president on his own before people started saying things was a wise decision.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.32). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 賢明な means "wise and appropriate"; it is mostly used as 賢明な判断 (decision) or 賢明な選択 (choice).
items.unit: 文脈規定 ナ形容詞

items.q: （ ）リズムに乗って、楽しく踊りましょう。
items.qr: (___) rizumu ni notte, tanoshiku odorimashou.
items.en: Let's move to the light, lively rhythm and dance and have fun.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.32). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 軽快な describes something that makes you feel pleasantly light. It can also describe light, quick-looking movements. (added, not in book) All four share 軽 — the "same kanji" trap. 軽率な is negative (thoughtless), 気軽な/手軽な are about ease.
items.unit: 文脈規定 ナ形容詞

items.q: 一つ問題が解決したと思ったら、（ ）問題が発生した。
items.qr: Hitotsu mondai ga kaiketsu shita to omottara, (___) mondai ga hassei shita.
items.en: Just when I thought one problem had been solved, a new one came up.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.32). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Written 新たな; it means the same as 新しい.
items.unit: 文脈規定 ナ形容詞

items.q: 大きな失敗をすると、だれでも（ ）気持ちになるものだ。
items.qr: Ookina shippai o suru to, dare demo (___) kimochi ni naru mono da.
items.en: When you make a big mistake, anyone ends up feeling gloomy.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.32). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): You can solve it once you notice that the person who fails and the person who feels ゆううつ are the same person. (added, not in book) めんどうな describes a task or a person you have to deal with, not the mood you are left in.
items.unit: 文脈規定 ナ形容詞

items.q: 彼女はモデルをしているだけあって、いつも（ ）服を着ている。
items.qr: Kanojo wa moderu o shite iru dake atte, itsumo (___) fuku o kite iru.
items.en: As you would expect of a model, she always wears chic clothes.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.32). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): It shows good taste and elegance (趣味がよく上品な様子).
items.unit: 文脈規定 ナ形容詞

items.q: あなたの発想は、ほかの人にはないとても（ ）ものですね。
items.qr: Anata no hassou wa, hoka no hito ni wa nai totemo (___) mono desu ne.
items.en: Your way of thinking is really unique — nobody else has ideas like that.

opts.en: (トーン "tone" is a noun; not used with な)
(ニュアンス "nuance" is a noun; not used with な)
(ユーモア "humour" is a noun; ユーモアのある is correct)

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.32). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): ほかの人にはない (that others don't have) is the hint.
items.unit: 文脈規定 ナ形容詞

items.q: 一人暮らしをしている子どものことを案じる親は多いものだ。
items.qr: Hitorigurashi o shite iru kodomo no koto o anjiru oya wa ooi mono da.
items.en: Many parents worry about their children who live on their own.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.36). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 案じる means 心配する (to worry), and it also has the meaning 考える (to think something out). Other options (added, not in book): none of 1–3 carries "worry": 意見する is telling someone off, 相談する is asking for advice, 遠慮する is holding back.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞①

items.q: 老人をもっといたわるべきだ。
items.qr: Roujin o motto itawaru beki da.
items.en: We should treat the elderly with more care.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.36). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): いたわる means 大事にする (to treat with care) and also やさしく接する (to treat gently). Other options (added, not in book): やしなう (養う) is supporting someone financially (家族を養う) — close, but it has no "gentle care" nuance. こだわる only sounds a little like いたわる.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞①

items.q: 自分の気持ちをすべて彼に打ち明けた。
items.qr: Jibun no kimochi o subete kare ni uchiaketa.
items.en: I told him everything I felt.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.36). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): for telling someone a secret or what you had in your heart without hiding it, 告白する means almost the same. Other options (added, not in book): 説明する is explaining facts or reasons — it lacks the "revealing something hidden" nuance of 打ち明ける.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞①

items.q: 忙しくて、返事を書くのを怠っていました。
items.qr: Isogashikute, henji o kaku no o okotatte imashita.
items.en: I was busy and neglected to write a reply.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.36). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 怠る has the meaning of 怠ける (namakeru), written with the same kanji 怠. さぼる (made from a foreign word; also written サボる) means the same. Other options (added, not in book): あせる and あわてる are about being rushed or flustered, not about not doing something; とぼける is pretending not to know.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞①

items.q: 秋の京都をおとずれる人はたくさんいる。
items.qr: Aki no Kyouto o otozureru hito wa takusan iru.
items.en: Many people visit Kyoto in autumn.

opts.en: to be based on, take into account

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.36). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 訪れる has the meaning of 訪ねる, written with the same kanji 訪. Other options (added, not in book): たずねる is also 尋ねる (to ask), but here it is 訪ねる. ひきいる (率いる) and ふまえる (踏まえる) are unrelated.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞①

items.q: 体力は、年齢とともに衰えていくものだ。
items.qr: Tairyoku wa, nenrei to tomo ni otoroete iku mono da.
items.en: Physical strength naturally declines with age.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.36). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): there is also the word 衰弱 (suijaku, weakening), which joins 衰 with the 弱 of 弱くなる. Other options (added, not in book): 薄くなる fits hair or colour (髪が薄くなる), not 体力.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞①

items.q: 我が社の社長は仕事の雰囲気を直接見たくて、現場に赴くことが多いそうだ。
items.qr: Waga sha no shachou wa shigoto no fun'iki o chokusetsu mitakute, genba ni omomuku koto ga ooi sou da.
items.en: I hear our company president often goes to the work sites because he wants to see the atmosphere for himself.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.36). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): a word using 赴 is 赴任 (funin), meaning "going to one's new post". Other options (added, not in book): 任せる is a trap built on the 任 of 赴任 — the compound means "go to a post", not "entrust".
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞①

items.q: タバコを吸うことは健康を害する行為である。
items.qr: Tabako o suu koto wa kenkou o gai suru koui de aru.
items.en: Smoking is an act that harms your health.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.36). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): there is also the word 損害 (songai, damage), which joins the 損 of 損なう with 害. 悪くする also means the same.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞①

items.q: 自分を成長させるには、自分をかえりみる時間を持つことが大事だ。
items.qr: Jibun o seichou saseru ni wa, jibun o kaerimiru jikan o motsu koto ga daiji da.
items.en: To grow as a person, it is important to have time to reflect on yourself.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.38). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): かえりみる can be written 省みる or 顧みる. Written 省みる it means the same as 反省する; written 顧みる it means the same as (昔のことを)振り返る, "look back on the past". Other options (added, not in book): with 自分を and 成長, the 省みる meaning (反省) is the one that fits.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞②

items.q: 今月は結婚式や飲み会が多く、出費がかさむ。
items.qr: Kongetsu wa kekkonshiki ya nomikai ga ooku, shuppi ga kasamu.
items.en: This month there are lots of weddings and drinking parties, so my expenses are piling up.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.38). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): かさむ is used when a quantity or an amount of money increases. Other options (added, not in book): 積もる is for things physically piling up (雪が積もる) — tempting, but it is not used with 出費.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞②

items.q: あきらめずに努力し続ければ、必ず夢はかなうものだ。
items.qr: Akiramezu ni doryoku shitsuzukereba, kanarazu yume wa kanau mono da.
items.en: If you keep working hard without giving up, your dream will surely come true.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.38). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): かなう means that a dream or wish is realised. It also has the meaning "to match an ideal or condition" (条件にかなう).
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞②

items.q: メーカー各社は、次世代の車をきそって開発している。
items.qr: Meekaa kakusha wa, jisedai no kuruma o kisotte kaihatsu shite iru.
items.en: Every manufacturer is competing to develop next-generation cars.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.38). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): in kanji it is written 競って, so 競争する is the closest meaning.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞②

items.q: ノートパソコンが1万円だなんて、これまでの常識を覆す価格だね。
items.qr: Nooto pasokon ga ichiman-en da nante, kore made no joushiki o kutsugaesu kakaku da ne.
items.en: A laptop for 10,000 yen? That price overturns everything we took for granted.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.38). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): read くつがえす. It means the same as ひっくりかえす, and is also used for "greatly changing a way of thinking that had been held to be correct".
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞②

items.q: 「品がない」という理由で、テレビの娯楽番組をけなす人は多い。
items.qr: "Hin ga nai" to iu riyuu de, terebi no goraku bangumi o kenasu hito wa ooi.
items.en: Many people run down TV entertainment shows as "tasteless".
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.38). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): けなす means almost the same as 悪く言う. Its opposite is ほめる (to praise). Other options (added, not in book): やっつける is beating an opponent, and 打ち消す is denying a statement — neither means criticising.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞②

items.q: わがままばかり言っていると、人間関係はこじれてしまうものだ。
items.qr: Wagamama bakari itte iru to, ningen kankei wa kojirete shimau mono da.
items.en: If you keep being selfish, your relationships will turn sour.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.38). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): こじれる means that a relationship or discussion gets tangled and stops going well, so here 悪化する is the closest meaning.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞②

items.q: 彼は料理教室に行って以来、料理にこっている。
items.qr: Kare wa ryouri kyoushitsu ni itte irai, ryouri ni kotte iru.
items.en: Ever since he went to a cooking class, he's been really into cooking.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.38). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): in the form 〜にこる it means 〜に夢中になる (to be absorbed in ~). Other options (added, not in book): こる (凝る) also means "to get stiff" (肩がこる) — a different use; しびれる (go numb) is a trap linked to that body meaning.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞②

items.q: 最近、何をやってもしくじってばかりで、元気が出ない。
items.qr: Saikin, nani o yatte mo shikujitte bakari de, genki ga denai.
items.en: Lately I keep messing up whatever I do, and I can't cheer up.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.40). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): しくじる means the same as 失敗する. Other options (added, not in book): 後悔する (regret) is what you might feel after failing, not the failing itself.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞③

items.q: 会社の命令にそむいて、自分だけの判断で行動した。
items.qr: Kaisha no meirei ni somuite, jibun dake no handan de koudou shita.
items.en: I went against the company's orders and acted on my own judgement.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.40). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): as the kanji 背く shows, it originally meant "to turn one's back on", and from that it came to mean 裏切る (betray), 反する (go against) and 逆らう (defy). Other options (added, not in book): 断る is refusing a request; it does not take 命令に and does not mean acting against an order.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞③

items.q: 最近、農業にたずさわる人が増えているそうだ。
items.qr: Saikin, nougyou ni tazusawaru hito ga fuete iru sou da.
items.en: I hear more and more people are going into farming these days.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.40). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): besides 関係する and かかわる, 従事する (to be engaged in) is also used with almost the same meaning.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞③

items.q: 田中先生からお祝いの言葉をたまわりたいと存じます。
items.qr: Tanaka-sensei kara oiwai no kotoba o tamawaritai to zonjimasu.
items.en: We would be honoured to receive a few words of congratulation from Professor Tanaka.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.40). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): like いただく, たまわる is the humble form of もらう, but たまわる is used in formal situations.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞③

items.q: インターネットに多くの時間を費やす人はかなり多い。
items.qr: Intaanetto ni ooku no jikan o tsuiyasu hito wa kanari ooi.
items.en: Quite a lot of people spend a great deal of time on the internet.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.40). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): read ついやす. It means almost the same as 使う, but is used mainly of money, labour and time, and also carries "keep using until it is gone" — in that sense there is 消費する.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞③

items.q: 看護師の資格を有する方を探しています。
items.qr: Kangoshi no shikaku o yuu suru kata o sagashite imasu.
items.en: We are looking for someone who holds a nursing qualification.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.40). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): besides 持っている, 所有する (to own) also has the same meaning. Other options (added, not in book): 目指している would mean the person does not have the qualification yet.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞③

items.q: 付き合っている二人を、周りの人たちがひやかした。
items.qr: Tsukiatte iru futari o, mawari no hitotachi ga hiyakashita.
items.en: The people around them teased the couple who were going out.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.40). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): besides "to tease" (からかう), ひやかす also means asking a shop clerk prices and so on with no intention of buying. Other options (added, not in book): ふざける is intransitive — you fool around yourself; you cannot ふざける someone (二人を).
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞③

items.q: 今年は、ホテルでクリスマスパーティーをもよおすそうです。
items.qr: Kotoshi wa, hoteru de kurisumasu paatii o moyoosu sou desu.
items.en: I hear that this year the Christmas party will be held at a hotel.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.40). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): it is written 催す in kanji, so it means almost the same as 開催する. It also has the meaning "to come into a state, to bring on", as in 吐き気をもよおす (to feel nauseous).
items.unit: 言い換え類義 動詞③

items.q: 面接は、意外とあっさり終わった。
items.qr: Mensetsu wa, igai to assari owatta.
items.en: The interview was over surprisingly quickly and easily.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.46). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): besides 簡単に, あっさり also means "light and fresh, not rich or heavy" (of a taste). Other options (added, not in book): しつこい is close to the opposite of あっさり (persistent; heavy taste).
items.unit: 言い換え類義 副詞

items.q: ドライブをするときには、あらかじめルートを決めておくとよい。
items.qr: Doraibu o suru toki ni wa, arakajime ruuto o kimete oku to yoi.
items.en: When you go for a drive, it's a good idea to decide your route in advance.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.46). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): written 予め in kanji; 予 carries the meaning 前もって, as in 予習 (preparing lessons) and 予報 (forecast).
items.unit: 言い換え類義 副詞

items.q: 試験に出ると予想したら、案の定そうなった。
items.qr: Shiken ni deru to yosou shitara, an no jou sou natta.
items.en: I predicted it would come up in the exam, and sure enough, it did.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.46). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): here 案 means 考え、思ったこと (an idea, what one thought) and 定 means 定まる、決まる (be settled), so 案の定 means 思ったとおり.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 副詞

items.q: あの選手は、引退した後も依然として人気がある。
items.qr: Ano senshu wa, intai shita ato mo izen to shite ninki ga aru.
items.en: That athlete is as popular as ever, even after retiring.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.46). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 依然 describes something unchanged from before. The word with the meaning "unchanged from before" is 相変わらず.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 副詞

items.q: この町は、かつて商人の町として栄えた。
items.qr: Kono machi wa, katsute shounin no machi to shite sakaeta.
items.en: This town once flourished as a merchant town.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.46). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): かつて means almost the same as むかし, 以前 and 前. Other options (added, not in book): もはや also points to time, but to "now, already" (もはや手遅れだ), the opposite direction.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 副詞

items.q: この印刷機は以前のものよりくっきり印刷できます。
items.qr: Kono insatsuki wa izen no mono yori kukkiri insatsu dekimasu.
items.en: This printer can print more sharply than the previous one.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.46). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): besides あざやかに, はっきり has roughly the same meaning. Other options (added, not in book): てっきり shares the -っきり sound but means "I was sure (but wrong)" (てっきり休みだと思った).
items.unit: 言い換え類義 副詞

items.q: 日本語はわかるが、英語はまるっきりわからない。
items.qr: Nihongo wa wakaru ga, eigo wa marukkiri wakaranai.
items.en: I understand Japanese, but I don't understand English at all.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.46). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): besides 全然, まったく also has the same meaning. Like 全然 and まったく, it is used together with a 〜ない expression. Other options (added, not in book): すっかり (すっかり忘れた) and めっきり (めっきり寒くなった) are used with positive verbs describing a change.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 副詞

items.q: 目下、卒業作品を制作中です。
items.qr: Mokka, sotsugyou sakuhin o seisakuchuu desu.
items.en: I'm currently working on my graduation piece.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.46). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): read もっか; it means 今のところ (for now). The word closest to this meaning is 現在. Other options (added, not in book): read めした, 目下 means "one's junior / subordinate" (目上 ⇔ 目下) — that is why 部下 and 上司 are among the options.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 副詞

items.q: あの人は怒るとおっかないから怒らせないほうがいいよ。
items.qr: Ano hito wa okoru to okkanai kara okorasenai hou ga ii yo.
