items.en: That person is scary when he gets angry, so you'd better not upset him.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.42). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): besides こわい, おそろしい also has almost the same meaning. Other options (added, not in book): ひどい describes cruel treatment or a bad state, not fear. Option 4 is faint in the scan; read as こい (濃い).
items.unit: 言い換え類義 イ形容詞

items.q: 彼女は、歌手としてはなばなしいデビューを飾った。
items.qr: Kanojo wa, kashu to shite hanabanashii debyuu o kazatta.
items.en: She made a brilliant debut as a singer.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.42). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): the はな of はなばなしい and the はな of はなやか both mean 花／華 (flower, splendour); both are expressions containing the meaning 見事な、立派な (splendid, fine). Other options (added, not in book): はなはだしい (甚だしい) only sounds similar — it means "extreme", usually about something bad (誤解もはなはだしい). はれやか (晴れやか) is a bright mood or face.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 イ形容詞

items.q: 日本は資源が乏しい国だといわれている。
items.qr: Nihon wa shigen ga toboshii kuni da to iwarete iru.
items.en: Japan is said to be a country poor in natural resources.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.42). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): besides 少ない, 足りない (not enough) or 不足している (insufficient) are used with almost the same meaning. Other options (added, not in book): 狭い would describe the land (国土が狭い), not 資源.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 イ形容詞

items.q: 外国語学習では、場面にふさわしい表現をたくさん覚えることが重要だ。
items.qr: Gaikokugo gakushuu de wa, bamen ni fusawashii hyougen o takusan oboeru koto ga juuyou da.
items.en: In foreign-language study, it is important to learn lots of expressions that suit each situation.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.42). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): ふさわしい means "matches the situation or atmosphere", so the closest meaning is ぴったりの. Other options (added, not in book): さっぱり, がっちり and あっさり are all ～り words of the same shape as ぴったり, but describe taste, build or manner.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 イ形容詞

items.q: 「ヒマラヤスギ」という木はスギではなくマツの仲間なので、紛らわしい。
items.qr: "Himarayasugi" to iu ki wa sugi de wa naku matsu no nakama na node, magirawashii.
items.en: The tree called "Himalayan cedar" (himaraya-sugi) is not actually a sugi (Japanese cedar) but a member of the pine family, so it is easy to get confused.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.42). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): read まぎらわしい; it means "easy to mistake because things are similar". おぼえにくい is a result of something being まぎらわしい, so it is not right as the answer.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 イ形容詞

items.q: 自分が悪いのにあやまりもせず、言い訳ばかりをするのはとても見苦しい。
items.qr: Jibun ga warui noni ayamari mo sezu, iiwake bakari o suru no wa totemo migurushii.
items.en: When you're the one at fault, making nothing but excuses without even apologising is really disgraceful.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.42). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): literally "painful to look at" (見るのが苦しい) — that is, it gives you an unpleasant feeling to watch. So the closest is みっともない. Another word with almost the same meaning is みにくい (醜い, ugly).
items.unit: 言い換え類義 イ形容詞

items.q: 今度の講演会には、世界的に名高い教授が来るそうだ。
items.qr: Kondo no kouenkai ni wa, sekaiteki ni nadakai kyouju ga kuru sou da.
items.en: I hear a world-famous professor is coming to the next lecture.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.42). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 高い has the meaning "widely known in the world", so 有名な means the same. 著名な (chomei na) is also the same. Other options (added, not in book): 1, 3 and 4 each share a kanji (名 or 高) with 名高い but mean something else — a typical shared-kanji trap.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 イ形容詞

items.q: 引っ越しのときには、しなくてはならない手続きがたくさんあり、わずらわしい。
items.qr: Hikkoshi no toki ni wa, shinakute wa naranai tetsuzuki ga takusan ari, wazurawashii.
items.en: When you move house there are so many procedures you have to do — it's a real hassle.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.42). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): written 煩わしい in kanji. It describes something complicated and bothersome, and is often used of procedures, methods and human relationships. Other options (added, not in book): つまらない (boring) is a different complaint — dull, not troublesome.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 イ形容詞

items.q: この地図は左右があべこべだ。
items.qr: Kono chizu wa sayuu ga abekobe da.
items.en: Left and right on this map are the wrong way round.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.44). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): あべこべな is used about order or position.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 ナ形容詞

items.q: かなり昔の映画なので、どんな内容だったかあやふやだ。
items.qr: Kanari mukashi no eiga na node, donna naiyou datta ka ayafuya da.
items.en: It's quite an old film, so I'm hazy about what it was about.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.44). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): あやふやな expresses that a thought or attitude is not clear; the nearest word is あいまいな. Other options (added, not in book): the tips page (p.8, in its 文脈規定 section) uses exactly this pair, あやふやな and あいまいな, as its example of words with close meanings.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 ナ形容詞

items.q: 「思う」と「考える」の違いを、おおざっぱに説明した。
items.qr: "Omou" to "kangaeru" no chigai o, oozappa ni setsumei shita.
items.en: I explained the difference between 思う and 考える in broad terms.
items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.44). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): おおざっぱ describes grasping the overall picture quickly without considering the details. Unlike おおまかな, it can also be used for personality. Other options (added, not in book): 丁寧に is the opposite idea (with care for detail).
items.unit: 言い換え類義 ナ形容詞

items.q: 財布を忘れて買い物にきた自分自身が、こっけいに思えた。
items.qr: Saifu o wasurete kaimono ni kita jibun jishin ga, kokkei ni omoeta.
items.en: Coming shopping without my wallet, I felt ridiculous.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.44). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): こっけい describes something so funny it might make you laugh — the same meaning as おかしい in the sense of おもしろい. Other options (added, not in book): くやしい (frustrated) is how you might also feel, but it is not the meaning of こっけい.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 ナ形容詞

items.q: 彼は勤勉で誠実な人です。
items.qr: Kare wa kinben de seijitsu na hito desu.
items.en: He is a hardworking and sincere person.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.44). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 誠実な means almost the same as まじめな. Other options (added, not in book): 熱心 is about eagerness; 誠実 is about honesty and good faith toward people.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 ナ形容詞

items.q: お客様の多様な要望におこたえするために努力いたします。
items.qr: Okyakusama no tayou na youbou ni okotae suru tame ni doryoku itashimasu.
items.en: We will do our best to meet our customers' diverse requests.
items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.44). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): besides いろいろな, さまざまな also has the same meaning.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 ナ形容詞

items.q: このパソコンは、頻繁に故障する。
items.qr: Kono pasokon wa, hinpan ni koshou suru.
items.en: This computer breaks down all the time.

opts.en: on the spur of the moment

items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.44). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): from its meanings "happening many times" and "done without a break", it equals しょっちゅう, which means ずっと、いつも. Other options (added, not in book): めったに is the opposite idea and needs a negative (めったに故障しない).
items.unit: 言い換え類義 ナ形容詞

items.q: 不審な人物を見たら警察に知らせてください。
items.qr: Fushin na jinbutsu o mitara keisatsu ni shirasete kudasai.
items.en: If you see a suspicious person, please tell the police.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.44). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): 不審 means feeling doubt because there is something unclear. The closest in meaning is あやしい. Other options (added, not in book): the answer is an い-adjective for a な-adjective — the "different part of speech" point from the tips page.
items.unit: 言い換え類義 ナ形容詞

items.q: 問1 欠陥は、即座に解決しなくてはならない。
items.qr: Kekkan wa, sokuza ni kaiketsu shinakute wa naranai.
items.en: The defect must be fixed immediately.

opts.en: not the reading of 欠陥
not the reading of 欠陥
not the reading of 欠陥

items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.10). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): 欠 (ケツ) + 陥 (カン): when ケツ is followed by a k-sound it shrinks to a small っ — けっかん. 1 forgets the 促音 (sokuon); 3/4 give 陥 a しょう reading it never has.

items.q: 問1 欠陥は、即座に解決しなくてはならない。
items.qr: Kekkan wa, sokuza ni kaiketsu shinakute wa naranai.
items.en: The defect must be fixed immediately.

opts.en: not the reading of 即座に
not the reading of 即座に
not the reading of 即座に

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.10). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): 即 is ソク (即座・即する), 座 is ザ. すぐに is the meaning, not the reading — a typical trap. ずいじ is 随時 (at any time), せいざ is 正座 (formal kneeling).

items.q: 問2 この苗を栽培するのは難しい。
items.qr: Kono nae o saibai suru no wa muzukashii.
items.en: Growing these seedlings is difficult.
items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.10). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): 苗 is read with its kun-yomi なえ (苗を植える). なわ is 縄 (rope), なお is 尚 (still more), なな is 七.

items.q: 問2 この苗を栽培するのは難しい。
items.qr: Kono nae o saibai suru no wa muzukashii.
items.en: Growing these seedlings is difficult.

opts.en: not the reading of 栽培
not the reading of 栽培
not the reading of 栽培

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.10). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): 栽 = サイ, 培 = バイ (栽培農家). さいばん is 裁判 (trial) — 栽 and 裁 look alike, so do not let the shared part pull you toward the wrong word. 培 is never ブ.

items.q: 問3 相手は依然として譲歩しないと言っている。
items.qr: Aite wa izen to shite jouho shinai to itte iru.
items.en: The other side says it still will not make any concession.

opts.en: not the reading of 依然
not the reading of 依然
not the reading of 依然
still, as before (依然として = still, as ever)

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.10). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): 依 is イ (依頼・依存). エ is a rare Buddhist reading (帰依 きえ) and never applies here. Note いぜん is also 以前 (before) — same sound, different word.

items.q: 問3 相手は依然として譲歩しないと言っている。
items.qr: Aite wa izen to shite jouho shinai to itte iru.
items.en: The other side says it still will not make any concession.

opts.en: not the reading of 譲歩
not the reading of 譲歩
not the reading of 譲歩

items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.10). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): 譲 is ジョウ (voiced, long vowel) and 歩 here is ホ (歩 has ホ／ボ／ブ). じょうぶ is 丈夫 (sturdy) and しょうぶ is 勝負 (match) — real words, so they look tempting.

items.q: 問4 新しい横綱は、前進するときの威力がかなりある。
items.qr: Atarashii yokozuna wa, zenshin suru toki no iryoku ga kanari aru.
items.en: The new yokozuna (sumo grand champion) has tremendous power when he pushes forward.

opts.en: not the reading of 横綱
not the reading of 横綱
not the reading of 横綱

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.10). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): An all-kun-yomi word: 横 よこ + 綱 つな → voiced to づな (連濁, rendaku). おう〜 tries an on-yomi (横 = オウ); あみ is 網 (net), which looks like 綱.

items.q: 問4 新しい横綱は、前進するときの威力がかなりある。
items.qr: Atarashii yokozuna wa, zenshin suru toki no iryoku ga kanari aru.
items.en: The new yokozuna (sumo grand champion) has tremendous power when he pushes forward.

opts.en: not the reading of 威力
not the reading of 威力
not the reading of 威力

items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.10). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): 威 = イ (権威・威張る); 力 here = リョク (as in 能力・努力). リキ appears in 力士 りきし / 自力 じりき, so 2 is a near miss. 威 is never えい.

items.q: 問5 腸の手術の経過は良好です。
items.qr: Chou no shujutsu no keika wa ryoukou desu.
items.en: Recovery after the intestinal surgery is going well.
items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.10). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): 腸 is チョウ (大腸・胃腸). The right side 昜 also appears in 場 (ジョウ), 湯 (トウ), 陽 (ヨウ) — exactly the "shared part" trap the tips page warns about.

items.q: 問5 腸の手術の経過は良好です。
items.qr: Chou no shujutsu no keika wa ryoukou desu.
items.en: Recovery after the intestinal surgery is going well.

opts.en: not the reading of 良好
not the reading of 良好
not the reading of 良好

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.10). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): 良 = リョウ (拗音 ryo, not yo) and 好 = コウ (long vowel, as in 友好・格好). 2 and 4 drop the long vowel of コウ.

items.q: 問6 不正乗車をした場合は、3倍の運賃を請求いたします。
items.qr: Fusei jousha o shita baai wa, sanbai no unchin o seikyuu itashimasu.
items.en: If you ride without a valid ticket, we will charge three times the fare.

opts.en: not the reading of 運賃
not the reading of 運賃
not the reading of 運賃

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.10). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): 賃 = チン (賃金・家賃). 賃 is not ニン (that is 任) and not キン (that is 金).

items.q: 問6 不正乗車をした場合は、3倍の運賃を請求いたします。
items.qr: Fusei jousha o shita baai wa, sanbai no unchin o seikyuu itashimasu.
items.en: If you ride without a valid ticket, we will charge three times the fare.

opts.en: not the reading of 請求
not the reading of 請求
not the reading of 請求

items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.10). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): 請 = セイ (要請・申請) and 求 = キュウ (要求). そきゅう is 遡及 (retroactive) — a real word, so it is the strongest distractor.

items.q: 問1 台風による災害の規模は、昔と比べると小さくなったが、それでも台風は恐ろしいものだ。
items.qr: Taifuu ni yoru saigai no kibo wa, mukashi to kuraberu to chiisaku natta ga, soredemo taifuu wa osoroshii mono da.
items.en: The scale of typhoon damage has become smaller than in the past, but typhoons are still frightening.

opts.en: not the reading of 災害
not the reading of 災害
not the reading of 災害

items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.12). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): 災 = サイ (天災), 害 = ガイ. ひがい is 被害 (damage suffered) and かがい is 加害 (inflicting harm) — real words with the same 害, so they tempt you. 災 contains 火 (fire), but it is not カ.

items.q: 問1 台風による災害の規模は、昔と比べると小さくなったが、それでも台風は恐ろしいものだ。
items.qr: Taifuu ni yoru saigai no kibo wa, mukashi to kuraberu to chiisaku natta ga, soredemo taifuu wa osoroshii mono da.
items.en: The scale of typhoon damage has become smaller than in the past, but typhoons are still frightening.

opts.en: not the reading of 規模
not the reading of 規模
not the reading of 規模

items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.12). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): 模 has two on-yomi — モ (模型・模様) and ボ, which is used in 規模. Option 2 picks the more common モ, the "several readings" trap. 規 = キ (規則), never きゅ.

items.q: 問2 大統領は、両国の合意を根底から覆す発言をした。
items.qr: Daitouryou wa, ryoukoku no goui o kontei kara kutsugaesu hatsugen o shita.
items.en: The president made a remark that overturned the two countries' agreement from its very foundation.

opts.en: not the reading of 根底
not the reading of 根底
not the reading of 根底

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.12). Why (added, not in book — the key gives numbers only): An on-yomi compound: 根 コン + 底 テイ (海底 かいてい). こんぽん is 根本 (root, basis) and ねもと is 根元 (base of a tree) — both real words with 根 and a similar meaning. ねそこ mixes kun-yomi ね + そこ (底).

items.q: (1) ほこる
items.qr: hokoru
items.en: She boasts the ability to be top in sales within the company.

opts.t: 彼女は社内営業成績トップの実力をほこっている。
opts.r: Kanojo wa shanai eigyou seiseki toppu no jitsuryoku o hokotte iru.
opts.en: She boasts the ability to be top in sales within the company.

opts.t: ほこったじゃがいもをつぶして、しょうゆとバターをつけて食べます。
opts.r: Hokotta jagaimo o tsubushite, shouyu to bataa o tsukete tabemasu.
opts.en: ✗ Means "mash steamed potatoes and eat them with soy sauce and butter" — needs ふかした (fukashita).

opts.t: 完ぺきな彼にも少しずつ欠点がほこり始めた。
opts.r: Kanpeki na kare ni mo sukoshi zutsu ketten ga hokori hajimeta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "flaws began to show even in perfect him" — needs 見え (mie) or ほころび (hokorobi, to come apart).

opts.t: 部屋を掃除しないと、すぐにほこってしまう。
opts.r: Heya o souji shinai to, sugu ni hokotte shimau.
opts.en: ✗ Means "the room soon gets dusty" — needs ほこりがたまって (hokori ga tamatte); ほこり "dust" is a noun, not this verb.

items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.48). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): ほこる expresses that someone or something has strength or force (here: real ability as the top seller). Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): 2 and 4 play on sound: ほこり (埃, dust) is a noun that looks like the verb's stem; 3 confuses it with ほころびる (綻びる, a seam coming apart → flaws showing). ほこる always takes something good as its object: 実力・

items.q: (2) たずさわる
items.qr: tazusawaru
items.en: While still a student, she is involved in interpreting work.

opts.r: Tazusawaranai han'i de kekkou na node, wakatte iru koto o oshiete moraemasu ka.
opts.en: ✗ Means "as far as it causes you no trouble, could you tell me what you know?" — needs さしつかえない (sashitsukaenai).

opts.t: 彼女は学生をしながら、通訳の仕事にたずさわっている。
opts.r: Kanojo wa gakusei o shinagara, tsuuyaku no shigoto ni tazusawatte iru.
opts.en: While still a student, she is involved in interpreting work.

opts.t: この金属は高熱をおびているので、たずさわることができない。
opts.r: Kono kinzoku wa kounetsu o obite iru node, tazusawaru koto ga dekinai.
opts.en: ✗ Means "this metal is very hot, so you cannot touch it" — needs さわる (sawaru).

opts.t: 彼は故郷の高校を卒業してから、一度も故郷をたずさわったことがない。
opts.r: Kare wa kokyou no koukou o sotsugyou shite kara, ichido mo kokyou o tazusawatta koto ga nai.
opts.en: ✗ Means "he has never once visited his hometown since high school" — needs おとずれた / たずねた (otozureta / tazuneta).

items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.48). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): たずさわる means being connected with some matter or job. 仕事にたずさわる is almost the same as 仕事をする. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): The pattern is always 〜に携わる with an activity (仕事・研究・活動). 3 borrows the さわる inside the word (touch); 4 borrows the たず of たずねる (visit) — and uses を, which たずさわる never takes.

opts.t: ふとした発言がきっかけで、隣の国との友好関係をそこなってしまった。
opts.r: Futo shita hatsugen ga kikkake de, tonari no kuni to no yuukou kankei o sokonatte shimatta.
opts.en: A careless remark ended up damaging friendly relations with the neighbouring country.

opts.t: もう少しで水泳がそこなうところだった。
opts.r: Mou sukoshi de suiei ga sokonau tokoro datta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "I almost drowned while swimming" — needs おぼれる (oboreru); そこなう needs an object, or a verb before it (〜しそこなう).

opts.t: 景気が悪くなると、そこなうまでは消費活動は停滞する。
opts.r: Keiki ga waruku naru to, sokonau made wa shouhi katsudou wa teitai suru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "once the economy worsens, spending stalls until it recovers" — needs 回復する (kaifuku suru).

opts.t: 花見のときは、大勢の見物客でそこなうことが多い。
opts.r: Hanami no toki wa, oozei no kenbutsukyaku de sokonau koto ga ooi.
opts.en: ✗ Means "at cherry-blossom time it is often crowded with visitors" — needs 混雑する / にぎわう (konzatsu suru / nigiwau).

items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.48). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): そこなう means "to hurt", "to fail", "to lose". As 〜しそこなう it also means "to come close to doing" or "to fail to do". Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): そこなう is transitive: something good (関係・健康・信用・機嫌) is the object with を. 2–4 use it with no object and with the meanings drown / recover / be crowded.

items.q: (4) つつしむ
items.qr: tsutsushimu
items.en: I respectfully offer my congratulations on the birth of your child.

opts.t: 住民の反対のために、工事の計画がなかなかつつしまない。
opts.r: Juumin no hantai no tame ni, kouji no keikaku ga nakanaka tsutsushimanai.
opts.en: ✗ Means "because residents object, the construction plan does not move forward" — needs 進まない (susumanai).

opts.t: お子さまの誕生を、つつしんでお喜び申し上げます。
opts.r: Okosama no tanjou o, tsutsushinde oyorokobi moushiagemasu.
opts.en: I respectfully offer my congratulations on the birth of your child.

opts.t: 割れそうな皿は、新聞紙でつつしんだほうがよい。
opts.r: Waresou na sara wa, shinbunshi de tsutsushinda hou ga yoi.
opts.en: ✗ Means "better wrap fragile plates in newspaper" — needs つつんだ (tsutsunda, 包む).

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.48). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Written 謹んで, meaning "with a composed, respectful feeling". つつしむ can also be written 慎む; then it means "to try not to do something, to hold back from doing it". Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): 4 is the sound trap: 包む (つつむ) "wrap" vs つつしむ. 1 and 2 have nothing to do with respect or restraint. Remember the fixed formal phrase つつしんで〜申

items.q: (5) おしよせる
items.qr: oshiyoseru
items.en: People who could not wait for opening time surged to the department-store entrance.

opts.t: 彼が、背中が痛いというので、背中をおしよせてみた。
opts.r: Kare ga, senaka ga itai to iu node, senaka o oshiyosete mita.
opts.en: ✗ Means "he said his back hurt, so I tried pressing / massaging it" — needs 押して / もんで (oshite / monde).

opts.t: 開店を待てない人々がデパートの入り口におしよせた。
opts.r: Kaiten o matenai hitobito ga depaato no iriguchi ni oshiyoseta.
opts.en: People who could not wait for opening time surged to the department-store entrance.

opts.t: これは多くの人からおしよせられた募金です。
opts.r: Kore wa ooku no hito kara oshiyoserareta bokin desu.
opts.en: ✗ Means "these are donations sent in by many people" — needs 寄せられた (yoserareta).

opts.t: 彼は多くの人の信用をおしよせられている。
opts.r: Kare wa ooku no hito no shin'you o oshiyoserarete iru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "he has the trust of many people" — needs 得て (ete) or 信頼を寄せられて (yoserarete).

items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.48). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Written 押し寄せる. Used like 波が押し寄せる (waves surge in); people can be likened to a wave, as in sentence 2. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): おしよせる is intransitive — a crowd or a wave is the subject and the destination takes に. 1 uses it transitively (背中を); 3 and 4 need plain 寄せる ("send in, give"), which only shares the second half.

items.q: (1) とりわけ
items.qr: toriwake
items.en: At today's international conference, the participants from Asia stood out in particular.

opts.t: 今話したことはとりわけ完成させてほしい。
opts.r: Ima hanashita koto wa toriwake kansei sasete hoshii.
opts.en: ✗ Means "I want what we just discussed finished without fail" — needs 必ず / ぜひ (kanarazu / zehi).

opts.t: 今日の国際会議はアジアからの参加者がとりわけ目立った。
opts.r: Kyou no kokusai kaigi wa Ajia kara no sankasha ga toriwake medatta.
opts.en: At today's international conference, the participants from Asia stood out in particular.

opts.t: 彼が連絡もなしに休んだのはなにかとりわけがあるはずだ。
opts.r: Kare ga renraku mo nashi ni yasunda no wa nani ka toriwake ga aru hazu da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "there must be some reason he was absent without notice" — needs わけ (wake, 訳) / 理由.

opts.t: 今年の試験はかなりとりわけだった。
opts.r: Kotoshi no shiken wa kanari toriwake datta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "this year's exam was quite special / difficult" — needs 特別 / 難しかった (tokubetsu / muzukashikatta); an adverb cannot be the predicate.

items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.58). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Same meaning as 特に / 特別に. It can also connect directly to a noun, as in とりわけ外国では ("especially abroad"), just like 特に. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): とりわけ picks one item out of a group and needs a predicate to modify (目立った). 3 hides the noun わけ ("reason") inside とりわけ; 4 uses it as a な-adjective, which it is not (特別 is).

items.q: (2) びっしょり
items.qr: bisshori
items.en: I have been running all this time, so I am drenched in sweat all over.

opts.t: 成績が上がらないために、部長にびっしょりと説教された。
opts.r: Seiseki ga agaranai tame ni, buchou ni bisshori to sekkyou sareta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "because my results didn't improve, I got a thorough lecture from the manager" — needs たっぷり / こってり (tappuri / kotteri).

opts.t: 神社の中は、人が多くてびっしょりとしている。
opts.r: Jinja no naka wa, hito ga ookute bisshori to shite iru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "the shrine is packed with people" — needs ぎっしり / ごった返して (gisshiri / gottagaeshite); びっしり also looks alike.

opts.t: ずっと走っていたので、全身にびっしょりと汗をかいている。
opts.r: Zutto hashitte ita node, zenshin ni bisshori to ase o kaite iru.
opts.en: I have been running all this time, so I am drenched in sweat all over.

opts.t: 私は、びっしょりした音楽はあまり好きではない。
opts.r: Watashi wa, bisshori shita ongaku wa amari suki de wa nai.
opts.en: ✗ Means "I don't much like wet, gloomy / heavy music" — needs しんみりした / じめじめした (shinmiri shita); びっしょり is only for things literally wet.

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.58). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): A word expressing "sweating a lot" and "being very wet from water, rain, etc." Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): The hint in 3 is 汗 (sweat). Onomatopoeia trap: びっしょり (wet) vs びっしり / ぎっしり (packed tight). Lectures (1) and music (4) cannot be wet.

items.q: (3) ぼうぜんと
items.qr: bouzen to
items.en: I didn't understand what had happened, and just stood there stunned.

opts.t: 店員として、ぼうぜんとした態度で対応してください。
opts.r: Ten'in to shite, bouzen to shita taido de taiou shite kudasai.
opts.en: ✗ Means "as a shop assistant, please deal with customers in a proper, composed manner" — needs きちんとした / 毅然とした (kichin to shita / kizen to shita).

opts.t: この問題はぼうぜんとしていて、どのように解決したらよいのかわからない。
opts.r: Kono mondai wa bouzen to shite ite, dono you ni kaiketsu shitara yoi no ka wakaranai.
opts.en: ✗ Means "this problem is so vague I don't know how to solve it" — needs 漠然と (bakuzen to).

opts.t: 雨がぼうぜんと降り始めた。
opts.en: ✗ Means "it began to rain heavily / suddenly" — needs ざあざあ / 猛烈に (zaazaa / mouretsu ni).

opts.t: 何が起こったのかわからなくて、ぼうぜんとしたままだった。
opts.r: Nani ga okotta no ka wakaranakute, bouzen to shita mama datta.
opts.en: I didn't understand what had happened, and just stood there stunned.

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.58). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Close to ぼんやりする, but used in situations where one has lost all energy and does not know what to do. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): ぼうぜんとする is a person's reaction to a shock. 2 is the sound-alike 漠然と (vague — for problems, plans, anxieties). Rain (3) and a work attitude (1) cannot be stunned.

items.q: (4) かろうじて
items.qr: karoujite
items.en: I didn't study much, but I only just passed the exam.

opts.t: あまり勉強しなかったが、試験にはかろうじて合格した。
opts.r: Amari benkyou shinakatta ga, shiken ni wa karoujite goukaku shita.
opts.en: I didn't study much, but I only just passed the exam.

opts.t: 彼が荷物をかろうじてくれたおかげで、とても助かった。
opts.r: Kare ga nimotsu o karoujite kureta okage de, totemo tasukatta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "it was a great help that he carried my bags" — needs かついで / 持って (katsuide / motte).

opts.t: 相手の外見だけでかろうじてはいけない。
opts.r: Aite no gaiken dake de karoujite wa ikenai.
opts.en: ✗ Means "you must not look down on / judge people by appearance alone" — needs 軽んじて / 判断して (karonjite / handan shite).

opts.t: 夜中までずっと勉強していたら、かろうじて眠くなってしまった。
opts.r: Yonaka made zutto benkyou shite itara, karoujite nemuku natte shimatta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "after studying until midnight I naturally / gradually got sleepy" — needs さすがに / だんだん (sasuga ni / dandan).

items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.58). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Shows being right on the borderline between "doing / becoming" and "not doing / not becoming". Can be replaced by なんとか or やっと. It also means ぎりぎりで (at the last moment) and often goes with 合格した, 間に合った. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): かろうじて is a hard-won success: かろうじて合格・間に合う・勝つ. 2 and 3 use it as a verb (〜てくれた, 〜てはいけない) — 3 is the s

items.q: (5) はなはだ
items.qr: hanahada
items.en: Forcing your own opinion on others as the right one is extremely annoying.

opts.t: 自分の意見を正しいとして押しつけるのははなはだ迷惑な話だ。
opts.r: Jibun no iken o tadashii to shite oshitsukeru no wa hanahada meiwaku na hanashi da.
opts.en: Forcing your own opinion on others as the right one is extremely annoying.

opts.t: 彼の性格は、考えなくてもはなはだわかる。
opts.r: Kare no seikaku wa, kangaenakute mo hanahada wakaru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "I can roughly / easily tell his character without thinking" — needs だいたい / すぐ (daitai / sugu).

opts.t: 近所の田中さんから、すてきなものをはなはだいただいた。
opts.r: Kinjo no Tanaka-san kara, suteki na mono o hanahada itadaita.
opts.en: ✗ Means "I received lots of lovely things from my neighbour Tanaka" — needs たくさん (takusan); はなはだ measures degree, not quantity.

opts.t: バスが動いているときに席を立つのは、はなはだですのでおやめください。
opts.r: Basu ga ugoite iru toki ni seki o tatsu no wa, hanahada desu node oyame kudasai.
opts.en: ✗ Means "standing up while the bus is moving is dangerous, so please don't" — needs 危険 (kiken); はなはだ alone cannot be the predicate (はなはだ危険です would work).

items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.58). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Means almost the same as ひじょうに or たいへん. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): はなはだ is a formal degree adverb placed before an adjective or a feeling — usually a negative one: はなはだ迷惑・残念・遺憾. It cannot count things (3), stand alone as a predicate (4), or modify わかる in the sense of "easily" (2).

items.q: (1) アクセル
items.qr: akuseru
items.en: Press the accelerator gently. It saves on petrol.

opts.t: インターネットを使うとさまざまな情報にアクセルすることができる。
opts.r: Intaanetto o tsukau to samazama na jouhou ni akuseru suru koto ga dekiru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "with the internet you can access all kinds of information" — needs アクセス (akusesu).

opts.t: 声が出にくいときは、このアクセルが効きますよ。
opts.r: Koe ga denikui toki wa, kono akuseru ga kikimasu yo.
opts.en: ✗ Means "when your voice is hoarse, this (throat) medicine works" — needs e.g. 薬 / のどあめ (kusuri / nodoame).

opts.t: アクセルはゆっくり踏みましょう。ガソリン代の節約になります。
opts.r: Akuseru wa yukkuri fumimashou. Gasorin dai no setsuyaku ni narimasu.
opts.en: Press the accelerator gently. It saves on petrol.

opts.t: アクセルは単語によって異なるので、辞書などで覚えるしかない。
opts.r: Akuseru wa tango ni yotte kotonaru node, jisho nado de oboeru shika nai.
opts.en: ✗ Means "the accent differs from word to word, so you can only learn it from a dictionary" — needs アクセント (akusento).

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.52). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): From English "accelerator pedal": the pedal used to speed up a car. アクセルを踏む is the common usage. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): 1 and 4 are katakana look-alikes: アクセス (access) and アクセント (accent). 2 has no connection to cars at all. The hint word in 3 is 踏む (press with the foot).

items.q: (2) ノイローゼ
items.qr: noiroze
items.en: After I gave my number to an estate agent, they call almost every day — it is driving me to a nervous breakdown.

opts.t: 社長は経営方針に不満を持ったので、午後の会議をノイローゼした。
opts.r: Shachou wa keiei houshin ni fuman o motta node, gogo no kaigi o noiroze shita.
opts.en: ✗ Means "the president was unhappy with the policy, so he boycotted the afternoon meeting" — needs ボイコット (boikotto).

opts.t: この小説のノイローゼは、主人公が一人でいろいろな問題を解決することだ。
opts.r: Kono shousetsu no noiroze wa, shujinkou ga hitori de iroiro na mondai o kaiketsu suru koto da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "the highlight / theme of this novel is the hero solving problems alone" — needs 見どころ / テーマ (midokoro / teema).

opts.t: 彼のノイローゼぶりにはだれもが困ってしまい、どうしようもできない状態だ。
opts.r: Kare no noiroze buri ni wa dare mo ga komatte shimai, dou shiyou mo dekinai joutai da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "everyone is at a loss with his selfishness" — needs わがまま (wagamama, わがままぶり).

opts.t: 不動産業者に電話番号を教えたら、毎日のように電話がかかってきてノイローゼにな[り]そうだ。
opts.r: Fudousan gyousha ni denwa bangou o oshietara, mainichi no you ni denwa ga kakatte kite noiroze ni nari sou da.
opts.en: After I gave my number to an estate agent, they call almost every day — it is driving me to a nervous breakdown.

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.52). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): From German "Neurose": a neurotic disorder in which one's feelings become unstable and one suffers. Also used for a state of worrying deeply. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): ノイローゼ is a condition you fall into — ノイローゼになる／ノイローゼ気味. It is not an action (1, ボイコット), not the content of a book (2), and not a personality trait shown in beha

items.q: (3) トーン
items.qr: toon
items.en: I want to change the colour of my room's walls to a calmer tone.

opts.t: 今日の料理のトーンは、肉か魚かどちらかをお選びいただけます。
opts.r: Kyou no ryouri no toon wa, niku ka sakana ka dochira ka o oerabi itadakemasu.
opts.en: ✗ Means "for today's main dish you may choose meat or fish" — needs メイン (mein).

opts.t: 道路の工事現場に、たくさんのトーンが置かれている。
opts.r: Douro no kouji genba ni, takusan no toon ga okarete iru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "many traffic cones are placed at the roadworks" — needs コーン (koon).

opts.t: このトーンを明日までに完成させないと、部長に怒られてしまう。
opts.r: Kono toon o ashita made ni kansei sasenai to, buchou ni okorarete shimau.
opts.en: ✗ Means "if I don't finish this (document / design) by tomorrow, the manager will be angry" — needs e.g. 資料 / デザイン (shiryou / dezain).

opts.t: 部屋の壁の色を、落ち着いたトーンに変えたいと思っている。
opts.r: Heya no kabe no iro o, ochitsuita toon ni kaetai to omotte iru.
opts.en: I want to change the colour of my room's walls to a calmer tone.

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.52). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): From English "tone": the tone or shade of a sound, voice or colour. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): The hint is 色 (colour) — トーン goes with 色・声・音 (明るいトーン, 声のトーンを落とす). 2 is the sound trap コーン (cone); 1 and 3 are not about sound or colour at all.

items.q: (4) デッサン
items.qr: dessan
items.en: My uncle drew me a beautiful sketch with just one pencil.

opts.t: おばさんにとって、食後に食べるデッサンが何よりもうれしいのだそうだ。
opts.r: Obasan ni totte, shokugo ni taberu dessan ga nani yori mo ureshii no da sou da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "for my aunt, the dessert after a meal is the greatest joy" — needs デザート (dezaato).

opts.t: おじさんは、鉛筆1本できれいなデッサンを描いてくれた。
opts.r: Ojisan wa, enpitsu ippon de kirei na dessan o kaite kureta.
opts.en: My uncle drew me a beautiful sketch with just one pencil.

opts.t: 久しぶりにデッサンに乗って出かけたが、とても楽しかった。
opts.r: Hisashiburi ni dessan ni notte dekaketa ga, totemo tanoshikatta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "I went out riding something for the first time in a while" — a vehicle (e.g. セダン sedan, ヨット yacht) is needed; you cannot ride a drawing.

opts.t: 毎日家のデッサンを開けたり閉めたりするのは大変なことだ。
opts.r: Mainichi ie no dessan o aketari shimetari suru no wa taihen na koto da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "opening and closing the house shutters every day is hard work" — needs シャッター (shattaa).

items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.52). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): From French "dessin": a picture drawn with a pencil or similar to capture an image. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): The hint is 鉛筆 + 描く. 1 is the sound trap デザート (dessert); 3 and 4 treat デッサン as a vehicle or a part of a house.

items.q: (5) ダウン
items.qr: daun
items.en: I collapsed (fell ill) from overwork.

opts.t: 社長のダウンのおかげで、業務の進行がスムーズになった。
opts.r: Shachou no daun no okage de, gyoumu no shinkou ga sumuuzu ni natta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "thanks to the president's leadership, work went smoothly" — needs リーダーシップ (riidaashippu); おかげで needs something positive.

opts.t: 彼は仕事もせずダウンな日々を送っている。
opts.r: Kare wa shigoto mo sezu daun na hibi o okutte iru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "he spends idle days without working" — needs 怠惰な / だらだらした (taida na / daradara shita); ダウン is not a な-adjective.

opts.t: 仕事のし過ぎでダウンしてしまった。
opts.r: Shigoto no shisugi de daun shite shimatta.

opts.t: 彼の言っていることは、まるでダウンだ。
opts.r: Kare no itte iru koto wa, marude daun da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "what he says is complete nonsense" — needs でたらめ / うそ (detarame / uso).

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.52). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): From English "down". Besides "lowering, dropping", it also means "collapsing, falling ill". Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): As a verb, ダウンする = to be knocked out / laid up (風邪でダウン, 過労でダウン); as a noun, a fall (イメージダウン, コストダウン). It is never a な-adjective (2) and does not mean nonsense (4).

items.q: (1) しぶとい
items.qr: shibutoi
items.en: This year's cold, once you catch it, just won't go away — it is quite stubborn.

opts.t: 彼女のしぶとい声が魅力的だ。
opts.r: Kanojo no shibutoi koe ga miryokuteki da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "her deep, mellow voice is attractive" — needs 渋い (shibui).

opts.t: この柿はしぶとくてにがい。
opts.en: ✗ Means "this persimmon is astringent and bitter" — needs 渋くて (shibukute).

opts.t: この部屋は、明るくてしぶとい。
opts.en: ✗ Means "this room is bright and spacious / comfortable" — needs 広い / 心地よい (hiroi / kokochiyoi).

opts.t: 今年の風邪は、かかるとなかなか治らず、結構しぶとい。
opts.r: Kotoshi no kaze wa, kakaru to nakanaka naorazu, kekkou shibutoi.
opts.en: This year's cold, once you catch it, just won't go away — it is quite stubborn.

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.54). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): The hint is なかなか〜ない. It describes something lasting longer than you expected. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): 1 and 2 are the sound trap 渋い (shibui: astringent taste / sober, mellow); しぶとい is about not giving up or not going away. A room (3) cannot be tenacious.

items.q: (2) もろい
items.qr: moroi
items.en: This chair is quite fragile, so please carry it carefully.

opts.t: もろい風が吹いて、飛ばされそうになった。
opts.r: Moroi kaze ga fuite, tobasaresou ni natta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "a strong wind blew and I was nearly blown away" — needs 強い / 激しい (tsuyoi / hageshii).

opts.t: もろいコーヒーは苦くて飲めない。
opts.en: ✗ Means "strong coffee is too bitter to drink" — needs 濃い (koi).

opts.t: このいすは、かなりもろいので、慎重に運んでください。
opts.r: Kono isu wa, kanari moroi node, shinchou ni hakonde kudasai.
opts.en: This chair is quite fragile, so please carry it carefully.

opts.t: 彼の作った料理は、いつも味がもろい。
opts.r: Kare no tsukutta ryouri wa, itsumo aji ga moroi.
opts.en: ✗ Means "his cooking always tastes bland" — needs 薄い (usui).

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.54). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Means "easily broken", "weak at withstanding force". Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): もろい describes physical objects (岩・ガラス・いす) or, figuratively, people's feelings (涙もろい "easily moved to tears", 情にもろい). It is not about wind, coffee strength or flavour. The hint in 3 is 慎重に運ぶ.

items.q: (3) だるい
items.qr: darui
items.en: I only sleep four hours a night, so my body feels unbearably heavy.

opts.t: 毎日4時間しか寝てないので、体がだるくてたまりません。
opts.r: Mainichi yojikan shika netenai node, karada ga darukute tamarimasen.
opts.en: I only sleep four hours a night, so my body feels unbearably heavy.

opts.t: 今日は朝からだるいので、気分がいい。
opts.r: Kyou wa asa kara darui node, kibun ga ii.
opts.en: ✗ Self-contradictory: "I feel sluggish, so I feel good." The meaning needs 調子がいい (choushi ga ii, "in good shape").

opts.t: あの人の性格は、私にとってはだるすぎます。
opts.r: Ano hito no seikaku wa, watashi ni totte wa darusugimasu.
opts.en: ✗ Means "that person's character is too harsh / gloomy for me" — needs e.g. きつ(すぎ) / 暗(すぎ); だるい is a body feeling, not a personality.

opts.t: このケーキは、あまりにもだるくて食べられない。
opts.r: Kono keeki wa, amari ni mo darukute taberarenai.
opts.en: ✗ Means "this cake is so sickly sweet I can't eat it" — needs 甘ったるくて (amattarukute).

items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.54). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): だるい is related to 疲れている (being tired) and is used as in 体がだるい. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): The subject of だるい is the body (体・足・腕). 4 is a clever trap: 甘ったるい ("cloyingly sweet") contains だるい-like sounds but is a different word.

items.q: (4) はかない
items.qr: hakanai
items.en: Precisely because life is fleeting, we should treasure it.

opts.t: 田中さんは、プロジェクトのリーダーにははかない人だ。
opts.r: Tanaka-san wa, purojekuto no riidaa ni wa hakanai hito da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "Tanaka is not suited to be project leader" — needs 向かない / 頼りない (mukanai / tayorinai).

opts.t: 彼女はよくないことがあったのか、ずっとはかない顔をしている。
opts.r: Kanojo wa yoku nai koto ga atta no ka, zutto hakanai kao o shite iru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "maybe something bad happened — she has looked gloomy all along" — needs 浮かない (ukanai).

opts.t: 彼が着ている上着、なかなかはかないですね。私もほしいなぁ。
opts.r: Kare ga kite iru uwagi, nakanaka hakanai desu ne. Watashi mo hoshii naa.
opts.en: ✗ Means "his jacket is really nice — I want one too" — needs すてき / いい (suteki / ii).

opts.t: 人生というものははかないからこそ、大切にするべきだ。
opts.r: Jinsei to iu mono wa hakanai kara koso, taisetsu ni suru beki da.
opts.en: Precisely because life is fleeting, we should treasure it.

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.54). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Used with words like 人生 (life), 命 (a life) and 恋 (love), meaning "does not last long". It also means "unlikely to come true", as in はかない希望 (a faint hope). Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): はかない collocates with things that end: 人生・命・恋・夢・希望. 2 is the look-alike 浮かない顔 (both end in 〜かない). It is not about suitability (1) or style (3).

items.q: (5) みすぼらしい
items.qr: misuborashii
items.en: He was dressed so shabbily that I didn't realise he was a famous actor.

opts.t: 山や森の新鮮な空気は、とてもみすぼらしい。
opts.r: Yama ya mori no shinsen na kuuki wa, totemo misuborashii.
opts.en: ✗ Means "the fresh mountain and forest air is very refreshing" — needs すがすがしい (sugasugashii).

opts.t: 久しぶりにふるさとに帰ってきて、みすぼらしくてうれしい気分だ。
opts.r: Hisashiburi ni furusato ni kaette kite, misuborashikute ureshii kibun da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "back home after a long time, I feel nostalgic and happy" — needs なつかしくて (natsukashikute).

opts.t: みすぼらしい格好をしていたので、その人が有名な俳優であることに気づかなかった。
opts.r: Misuborashii kakkou o shite ita node, sono hito ga yuumei na haiyuu de aru koto ni kizukanakatta.
opts.en: He was dressed so shabbily that I didn't realise he was a famous actor.

opts.t: 部屋をきれいにしたら、気分がだんだんみすぼらしくなってきた。
opts.r: Heya o kirei ni shitara, kibun ga dandan misuborashiku natte kita.
opts.en: ✗ Means "after cleaning the room I gradually felt refreshed" — needs すがすがしく / さっぱり (sugasugashiku / sappari).

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.54). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Expresses that the outward appearance (how something looks) is poor. Often used for a person's clothes or a building's exterior. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): みすぼらしい is negative and visual — 格好・服・家・建物. 1, 2 and 4 are all positive feelings, so a negative appearance word cannot fit.

items.q: (1) めど
items.qr: medo
items.en: I have written up everything needed. Now handing in the report is in sight.

opts.t: 彼女は絵画の価値を見分けるめどを持っている。
opts.r: Kanojo wa kaiga no kachi o miwakeru medo o motte iru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "she has an eye for judging the value of paintings" — needs 目 (me) / 目利きの力.

opts.t: 必要な内容をすべて書き上げた。これでレポート提出のめどが立った。
opts.r: Hitsuyou na naiyou o subete kakiageta. Kore de repooto teishutsu no medo ga tatta.
opts.en: I have written up everything needed. Now handing in the report is in sight.

opts.t: そんな料理をレストランのメニューにするなんて、めどにもならない。
opts.r: Sonna ryouri o resutoran no menyuu ni suru nante, medo ni mo naranai.
opts.en: ✗ Means "putting such a dish on a restaurant menu is out of the question" — needs 話にもならない (hanashi ni mo naranai).

opts.t: するかしないかを決断するには、はっきりとしためどを持つことが大切である。
opts.r: Suru ka shinai ka o ketsudan suru ni wa, hakkiri to shita medo o motsu koto ga taisetsu de aru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "to decide whether to do it, a clear criterion is important" — needs 基準 (kijun).

items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.50). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Often used in the forms めどが立つ / めどがつく, meaning "the schedule becomes clear; how things will go from now can be foreseen". Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): めど is the point you are heading for and whether you can see it. It is not an ability (1 = 目), not a judgment standard (4 = 基準), and has no idiom めどにもならない (3).

items.q: (2) つじつま
items.qr: tsujitsuma
items.en: In this film, the story in the first half and the second half does not add up.

opts.t: 彼の演説はさっきからつじつまだらけだ。
opts.r: Kare no enzetsu wa sakki kara tsujitsuma darake da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "his speech has been full of contradictions" — needs 矛盾 (mujun); つじつま is the consistency itself.

opts.t: 面接のときは、服のつじつまに注意したほうがいい。
opts.r: Mensetsu no toki wa, fuku no tsujitsuma ni chuui shita hou ga ii.
opts.en: ✗ Means "at an interview, pay attention to how you are dressed" — needs 身だしなみ / 着こなし (midashinami / kikonashi).

opts.t: この映画は前半と後半で話のつじつまが合わない。
opts.r: Kono eiga wa zenhan to kouhan de hanashi no tsujitsuma ga awanai.
opts.en: In this film, the story in the first half and the second half does not add up.

opts.t: 彼女はさっきからつじつまがない表情をしていて、さみしそうだ。
opts.r: Kanojo wa sakki kara tsujitsuma ga nai hyoujou o shite ite, samishisou da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "she has looked downcast for a while and seems lonely" — needs 元気がない / 浮かない (genki ga nai / ukanai).

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.50). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): The proper line of reasoning that should run through something; the right way. Most often in つじつまが合う / 合わない. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): つじつま belongs to stories, explanations and arguments, almost always with 合う／合わない (or つじつまを合わせる "make the story fit"). It never describes clothes (2) or a face (4), and "full of つじつま" (1) would

items.q: (3) 本場
items.qr: honba
items.en: Korea is the home of kimchi.

opts.t: 本場になると、緊張してしまう。
opts.r: Honba ni naru to, kinchou shite shimau.
opts.en: ✗ Means "when the real performance comes, I get nervous" — needs 本番 (honban).

opts.t: 図書館にある本場は高さが高い。
opts.r: Toshokan ni aru honba wa takasa ga takai.
opts.en: ✗ Means "the bookshelves in the library are tall" — needs 本棚 (hondana).

opts.t: 事件本場にたくさんの警察官が集まっている。
opts.r: Jiken honba ni takusan no keisatsukan ga atsumatte iru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "many police officers are gathered at the scene of the incident" — needs 現場 (genba).

opts.t: キムチは、韓国が本場だ。
opts.r: Kimuchi wa, Kankoku ga honba da.
opts.en: Korea is the home of kimchi.

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.50). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Refers to a place famous for a food or product. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): All three wrong options swap in a word sharing one kanji or sound: 本番 (honban, the real performance), 本棚 (hondana, bookshelf), 現場 (genba, the scene). 本場 is about where something is authentic: 本場の味, 本場仕込み.

items.q: (4) ずれ
items.qr: zure
items.en: There is a gap between our company's management policy and that company's.

opts.t: ズボンのずれが汚れていますよ。
opts.r: Zubon no zure ga yogorete imasu yo.
opts.en: ✗ Means "the hem of your trousers is dirty" — needs すそ (suso).

opts.t: 我が社とあの会社との経営方針にはずれがある。
opts.r: Waga sha to ano kaisha to no keiei houshin ni wa zure ga aru.
opts.en: There is a gap between our company's management policy and that company's.

opts.t: 傘をささないで歩いていたら、雨でずれになってしまった。
opts.r: Kasa o sasanaide aruite itara, ame de zure ni natte shimatta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "I walked without an umbrella and got soaked" — needs ずぶぬれ (zubunure).

opts.t: お金がないので、あの人のずれにお世話になることになった。
opts.r: Okane ga nai node, ano hito no zure ni osewa ni naru koto ni natta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "I have no money, so I will be staying at that person's place" — needs ところ (tokoro).

items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.50). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): The noun form of the verb ずれる; it means not lining up with one's own opinion, way of thinking or sense of things. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): ずれ is an abstract gap between two things (方針・意見・感覚・時間のずれ) or a physical slip out of place. 3 tries to use ずぶぬれ, which only starts with the same sound; 1 and 4 need concrete nouns (すそ, ところ

items.q: (5) 台無し
items.qr: dainashi
items.en: Just one mistake ruined a plan that had been going smoothly.

opts.t: たった一つのミスで、順調にいっていた計画が台無しになってしまった。
opts.r: Tatta hitotsu no misu de, junchou ni itte ita keikaku ga dainashi ni natte shimatta.
opts.en: Just one mistake ruined a plan that had been going smoothly.

opts.t: 最近、どうも台無しが多いと思っているうちに、機械が故障してしまった。
opts.r: Saikin, doumo dainashi ga ooi to omotte iru uchi ni, kikai ga koshou shite shimatta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "I thought there had been a lot of glitches lately, and then the machine broke" — needs 不具合 (fuguai).

opts.t: 台無しのうちは、まだ大丈夫だから心配しないでください。
opts.r: Dainashi no uchi wa, mada daijoubu dakara shinpai shinaide kudasai.
opts.en: ✗ Self-contradictory: 台無し is the end state of total ruin, so "while it is ruined it's still fine" makes no sense — something like この程度 (kono teido, "at this level") was meant.

opts.t: 彼の台無しに対してあれこれ言うのはよくないことだ。
opts.r: Kare no dainashi ni taishite are kore iu no wa yoku nai koto da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "it is not good to criticise his failure" — needs 失敗 (shippai).

items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.50). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Means that something ends up ruined. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): 台無し is a result, not an event: the thing that was good (計画・苦労・せっかくの休日) is the subject, in 〜が台無しになる／〜を台無しにする. It cannot be counted (2 "many 台無し") or belong to a person as "his failure" (4).

items.q: (1) きゃしゃな
items.qr: kyasha na
items.en: She looks delicate, but she is very strong.

opts.t: ほかの人の意見を聞くと、きゃしゃに考えが変わることがある。
opts.r: Hoka no hito no iken o kiku to, kyasha ni kangae ga kawaru koto ga aru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "when I hear others' opinions my mind sometimes changes easily" — needs 簡単に / すぐに (kantan ni / sugu ni).

opts.t: きゃしゃな話だから、すぐに信用することはできない。
opts.r: Kyasha na hanashi dakara, sugu ni shin'you suru koto wa dekinai.
opts.en: ✗ Means "it is a dubious story, so I can't trust it right away" — needs あやしい / うさんくさい (ayashii / usankusai).

opts.t: あのおばあさんは80歳を過ぎても元気で、とてもきゃしゃだ。
opts.r: Ano obaasan wa hachijussai o sugite mo genki de, totemo kyasha da.
opts.en: ✗ Contradiction: she is lively at over 80, so the sense is "very sturdy / healthy" — needs 丈夫だ / 達者だ (joubu da / tassha da).

opts.t: 彼女は見かけはきゃしゃだが、とても力がある。
opts.r: Kanojo wa mikake wa kyasha da ga, totemo chikara ga aru.
opts.en: She looks delicate, but she is very strong.

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.56). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Means "thin and weak-looking"; used both in a good sense and in a bad sense. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): きゃしゃ describes a visible build — of a person, a chair, a wrist. The hint in 4 is 見かけは〜が (looks … but). It cannot describe how a thought changes (1) or how believable a story is (2), and 3 needs the opposite meaning.

items.q: (2) ゆるやかな
items.qr: yuruyaka na
items.en: According to economists, the economy will gradually head towards recovery.

opts.t: コンサート会場に、立派でゆるやかな歌声が響いた。
opts.r: Konsaato kaijou ni, rippa de yuruyaka na utagoe ga hibiita.
opts.en: ✗ Means "a fine, rich / free-flowing singing voice rang out in the concert hall" — needs 伸びやかな / 豊かな (nobiyaka na / yutaka na).

opts.t: 温泉に入ると、気持ちがゆるやかになりますね。
opts.r: Onsen ni hairu to, kimochi ga yuruyaka ni narimasu ne.
opts.en: ✗ Means "getting into a hot spring makes you feel calm / relaxed" — needs おだやかに / のんびりした気分に (odayaka ni).

opts.t: 経済の専門家によると、景気はゆるやかに回復に向かっていくそうだ。
opts.r: Keizai no senmonka ni yoru to, keiki wa yuruyaka ni kaifuku ni mukatte iku sou da.
opts.en: According to economists, the economy will gradually head towards recovery.

opts.t: 彼はゆるやかな性格で、ほとんど怒ることがないそうだ。
opts.r: Kare wa yuruyaka na seikaku de, hotondo okoru koto ga nai sou da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "he has a mild temperament and almost never gets angry" — needs おだやかな / おおらかな (odayaka na / ooraka na).

items.why: Answer 3 (book key, p.56). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Written 緩やか. ゆるやかに means nearly the same as ゆっくり (slowly) or 徐々に (gradually). Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): ゆるやか describes a rate of change or a slope: ゆるやかな坂・流れ・カーブ, ゆるやかに回復する／上昇する. Calm feelings and a mild temperament are おだやか (2, 4) — this is the trap that catches English speakers, since both are "gentle" in English.

items.q: (3) ぞんざいな
items.qr: zonzai na
items.en: He has a rough, careless way of speaking.

opts.t: 我が社のぞんざいに関わる大きな問題である。
opts.r: Waga sha no zonzai ni kakawaru ookina mondai de aru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "this is a big problem that concerns our company's existence / survival" — needs 存続 / 存亡 (sonzoku / sonbou); そんざい (存在) only sounds alike.

opts.t: 彼は話し方がぞんざいだ。
opts.r: Kare wa hanashikata ga zonzai da.
opts.en: He has a rough, careless way of speaking.

opts.t: この本は難しいので、読むとぞんざいな気持ちになる。
opts.r: Kono hon wa muzukashii node, yomu to zonzai na kimochi ni naru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "this book is hard, so reading it makes me feel fed up / depressed" — needs うんざりした / ゆううつな (unzari shita / yuuutsu na).

opts.t: 卵をかき混ぜると、じょじょにぞんざいになっていきます。
opts.r: Tamago o kakimazeru to, jojo ni zonzai ni natte ikimasu.
opts.en: ✗ Means "as you beat the eggs they gradually become smooth / fluffy" — needs なめらかに / ふんわり (nameraka ni / funwari).

items.why: Answer 2 (book key, p.56). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): ぞんざいな carries the meaning of いいかげん (slapdash), or of 乱暴 (rough) and 失礼 (rude). Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): ぞんざい describes how someone treats things or people: 話し方・扱い・返事・態度がぞんざい. 1 is the sound trap そんざい (存在) → 存続; 3 and 4 are about feelings and food texture.

items.q: (4) きらびやかな
items.qr: kirabiyaka na
items.en: Every year that singer performs in a dazzling costume.

opts.t: この町もずいぶんきらびやかになったものだなぁ。
opts.r: Kono machi mo zuibun kirabiyaka ni natta mono da naa.
opts.en: ✗ Means "this town has really become lively / bustling" — needs にぎやかに / 華やかに (nigiyaka ni / hanayaka ni).

opts.t: 今年もきらびやかに運動会が行われた。
opts.r: Kotoshi mo kirabiyaka ni undoukai ga okonawareta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "the sports day was held in grand / lively style again this year" — needs 盛大に / にぎやかに (seidai ni).

opts.t: 彼女はきらびやかな声を持っている。
opts.r: Kanojo wa kirabiyaka na koe o motte iru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "she has a clear, beautiful voice" — needs 澄んだ / 美しい (sunda / utsukushii); きらびやか is visual.

opts.t: あの歌手は毎年きらびやかな衣装を着て歌を歌う。
opts.r: Ano kashu wa maitoshi kirabiyaka na ishou o kite uta o utau.
opts.en: Every year that singer performs in a dazzling costume.

items.why: Answer 4 (book key, p.56). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Describes something shining. Used mainly about appearance and dress. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): きらびやか = glittering to the eye: 衣装・装飾・宝石. 1 and 2 describe liveliness (にぎやか), 3 is a sound — none of them glitter.

items.q: (5) 明瞭な
items.qr: meiryou na
items.en: The new English teacher's pronunciation is very clear and easy to understand.

opts.t: 新しい英語の先生の発音はとても明瞭で、わかりやすい。
opts.r: Atarashii eigo no sensei no hatsuon wa totemo meiryou de, wakariyasui.
opts.en: The new English teacher's pronunciation is very clear and easy to understand.

opts.t: 日が長くなると、夜遅くまで空が明瞭だ。
opts.r: Hi ga nagaku naru to, yoru osoku made sora ga meiryou da.
opts.en: ✗ Means "when the days get longer, the sky stays light until late" — needs 明るい (akarui).

opts.t: 彼女は法律に関して明瞭な知識を持っている。
opts.r: Kanojo wa houritsu ni kanshite meiryou na chishiki o motte iru.
opts.en: ✗ Means "she has thorough / accurate knowledge of the law" — needs 豊富な / 正確な (houfu na / seikaku na).

opts.t: 物語を読み進むにつれ、登場人物のなぞが明瞭になっていった。
opts.r: Monogatari o yomisusumu ni tsure, toujou jinbutsu no nazo ga meiryou ni natte itta.
opts.en: ✗ Means "as I read on, the characters' mystery was gradually revealed" — needs 明らかに (akiraka ni).

items.why: Answer 1 (book key, p.56). Book's 解説 (paraphrased): Means the same as 明らかだ / はっきりしている, but the words it can be used with are limited: 内容 (content), 意識 (consciousness), 意味 (meaning), 音 (sound), 言葉 (words) and so on. Why the others are wrong (added, not in book): 明瞭 is about being clearly perceived — a sound, words, a meaning (発音・発言・意識が明瞭). A mystery "being revealed" (4) is 明らかになる, the light sky (2)
